definition_zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；监测；监控；监听
definition_en: a device that displays or records information, a person who warns or keeps order, or to watch and check something continuously over time
core_image: 一个站在旁边不断提醒“注意”的人，眼睛一直盯着同一处
scene: 控制室里，工程师盯着显示管道压力的监视器。From the control room the engineer watched the monitor that showed the pressure inside the pipeline.
sceneCN: 这里 monitor 是「显示器」（第 1 个义项：显示画面或数据的屏幕）；句意：工程师在控制室里盯着显示管道内压力的显示器。场景要点：昏暗的控制室、一排亮着的屏幕、屏幕上跳动的压力曲线、管道剖面图；对应第 1 个义项。

监测；监控；监听；跟踪观察

senses.title: A screen that shows the picture
senses.definition: a screen, especially a computer or television display, that shows information or a picture
senses.definitionCN: 显示信息或画面的屏幕，尤指电脑或电视显示屏
senses.example: The second monitor shows the camera feed from the front door.
senses.exampleCN: 第二块显示器显示前门的摄像头画面。
senses.why: Broadcasting used a monitor for a device that continuously checked a transmission, and the screen showing that check took the name. A computer display repeats the role: it lets someone keep watch on what the machine is doing.
senses.whyCN: 广播业曾把持续检查传输质量的设备称为 monitor，显示这项检查的屏幕便沿用了这个名字。电脑显示器重复着同一角色：让人持续看清机器在做什么。

senses.title: An instrument that keeps watch
senses.definition: a device that continuously measures and displays a physical condition, such as heart rate or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 持续测量并显示某项身体或物理状况的设备，如心率或压力
senses.example: The heart monitor began to beep faster and faster.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏监测仪开始越响越快地鸣叫。
senses.why: The Latin monitor was a person who warned. An instrument that watches a pulse and sounds an alarm takes over the warning job, so the person's title passes to the machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 是一个发出警告的人。一台盯着脉搏、并发出警报的仪器接过了这份警告的职责，于是人的称呼转移到了机器上。

senses.title: The pupil who keeps order
senses.definition: a senior pupil at a school given the task of keeping order or checking attendance
senses.definitionCN: 学校里被赋予维持秩序或检查出勤任务的高年级学生
senses.example: The hall monitor checked the corridors every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊值日生每小时巡查一次走廊。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense, from 1540s: a senior pupil 'charged with keeping order'. The student does exactly what the Latin word says — reminds others of the rules and reports breaches.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项，始于 16 世纪 40 年代：受命维持秩序的高年级学生。这个学生做的正是拉丁词所说的——提醒别人守规矩，并报告违规。

senses.title: An official who warns
senses.definition: a person appointed to observe, advise, and warn, especially in an official or technical role
senses.definitionCN: 受指派观察、建议并提出告诫的人，尤指担任正式或技术职务者
senses.example: A monitor was appointed to warn the committee about conflicts of interest.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会任命了一名监督员，就利益冲突提出告诫。
senses.why: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide'. The English noun keeps that advisory, warning figure before it ever names a machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人”。英语名词先保留了这个提出建议与警告的人，之后才用它命名机器。

senses.title: Watch the numbers over time
senses.definition: to measure and check a quantity or condition regularly over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内定期测量并检查某个数量或状况
senses.example: Sensors monitor the temperature of the tank every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器每十分钟监测一次储罐的温度。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1924 for checking the quality of radio signals. Its core is repetition: a monitor does not look once but keeps looking, so the verb means sustained checking rather than a single glance.
senses.whyCN: 动词于 1924 年出现，指检查无线电信号的质量。它的核心是重复：monitor 不是看一眼，而是持续地看，所以这个动词表示持续的检查，而不是一瞥。

senses.title: Keep someone under surveillance
senses.definition: to watch a person, group, or activity closely, especially to detect wrongdoing or risk
senses.definitionCN: 密切注视某人、某群体或某项活动，尤为了发现不当行为或风险
senses.example: The company monitors its drivers' speed and braking through an app.
senses.exampleCN: 公司通过一个应用监控司机的车速与刹车情况。
senses.why: When the watching is turned from a gauge to people, the warning role becomes surveillance. The same continuous attention is now aimed at behaviour that may need correcting.
senses.whyCN: 当注视的对象从仪表转向人，提醒的职责就变成了监控。同样的持续关注，现在对准了可能需要纠正的行为。

senses.title: Listen to a channel
senses.definition: to listen to a radio, telephone, or other channel continuously in order to catch particular information
senses.definitionCN: 持续收听无线电、电话或其他频道，以捕捉特定信息
senses.example: They monitored the radio channel all night, waiting for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整夜监听那个无线电频道，等待回复。
senses.why: The earliest verb sense was exactly this: checking radio signals for quality. Listening to a channel is watching with the ears, and the word's continuity remains.
senses.whyCN: 最早的动词义正是这个：检查无线电信号的质量。用耳朵听一个频道就是“用耳朵看”，而这个词的持续性仍然保留。

senses.title: The lizard that warns
senses.definition: a large lizard of the family Varanidae, called a monitor because of an old story that it warned people of crocodiles
senses.definitionCN: 巨蜥科的大型蜥蜴，因古老传说称它会向人预警鳄鱼而得名
senses.example: A monitor lizard crossed the trail and disappeared into the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只巨蜥穿过小径，消失在草丛里。
senses.why: The name was given in 1826 because the lizard was fabled to give warning of Nile crocodiles. It is the same 'warner' sense, applied to an animal rather than a person or device.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字始于 1826 年，因为传说这种蜥蜴会预警尼罗河鳄鱼。它仍是“警告者”这层意思，只是用在了动物身上，而不是人或设备。

senses.title: The ironclad that admonished
senses.definition: the name of the first ironclad warship of that design, built in 1862 and intended as a warning to the Confederacy
senses.definitionCN: 1862 年建造的第一艘该型铁甲舰的名称，意在向南方邦联发出警告
senses.example: The Monitor fought the Merrimack in 1862 and changed naval warfare.
senses.exampleCN: 1862 年，莫尼特号与梅里马克号交战，改变了海战方式。
senses.why: The inventor chose the name because the ship was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders. The Latin warner becomes a floating threat, a warning made of iron.
senses.whyCN: 发明者选择这个名字，是因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。拉丁语的告诫者变成了浮在水上的威胁，一个用铁铸成的警告。

senses.title: A background watcher in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的后台监控程序
senses.definition: in computing, a program or process that runs in the background and checks system activity
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指在后台运行、检查系统活动的程序或进程
senses.example: A background monitor logs every login and flags unusual hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个后台监控程序记录每次登录，并标记异常时段。
senses.why: Software repeats the human watchman: it runs unnoticed, checks continuously, and reports what looks wrong. The old 'one who warns' is now a loop of code.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复着人类更夫的角色：它不声不响地运行，持续检查，并报告看起来不对的地方。古老的“告诫者”如今成了一段循环的代码。

intro.en: Monitor began as a Latin word for a person who warns, entered English in the sixteenth century as a school officer, and only in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries became a machine, a lizard, a warship, and finally a screen. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monitor 最初是拉丁语中表示“告诫者”的词，16 世纪作为学校职务进入英语，直到 19 与 20 世纪才变成仪器、蜥蜴、军舰，最后成为屏幕。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'senior pupil at a school charged with keeping order'. It came from Latin monitor.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“受命维持秩序的学校高年级学生”。它来自拉丁语 monitor。

items.en: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide, teacher'. It was an agent noun from monere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人、教师”。它是 monere 的施动名词。

items.en: Monere meant 'to remind, bring to one's recollection, tell of; admonish, advise, warn, instruct, teach'. It goes back to PIE *moneie-, a causative form of *men- 'to think', the root also behind Latin memini 'I remember' and mens 'mind'.
items.cn: monere 意为“提醒、使想起、告知；告诫、建议、警告、指导、教导”。它可追溯到原始印欧语 *moneie-，即 *men-“思考”的使役形式；同一词根也是拉丁语 memini“我记得”与 mens“心智”的来源。

items.en: The monitor lizard was so called because it was fabled to warn people of Nile crocodiles (1826). The ironclad warship Monitor (1862) was named by its inventor because it was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders.
items.cn: 巨蜥被称为 monitor，是因为传说它会向人预警尼罗河鳄鱼（1826）。铁甲舰莫尼特号（1862）由发明者命名，因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。

items.en: The verb is recorded in 1924 meaning 'to check for quality', originally of radio signals. The general sense 'observe, keep under review' is from 1944. Keats had used it in 1818 to mean 'to guide'.
items.cn: 动词于 1924 年有记录，意为“检查质量”，最初用于无线电信号。泛指“观察、持续审视”的义项始于 1944 年。济慈在 1818 年曾用它表示“引导”。

items.en: A broadcasting sense, 'a device to continuously check on the technical quality of a transmission', is recorded from 1931 and led to the sense 'a TV screen displaying the picture from a particular camera'. The computer display is a later extension of that screen sense.
items.cn: 广播义“持续检查传输技术质量的设备”记录于 1931 年，并由此引出“显示某一摄像机画面的电视屏幕”这一义项。电脑显示器是该屏幕义的后期引申。

note.en: The first group separates the noun and adjective forms built on monitor from two related warning words; the second compares the verbs of watching that learners use interchangeably.
note.cn: 第一组把由 monitor 构成的名词与形容词形式，同两个相关的“警告”词分开；第二组比较学习者常互换使用的几个“看管”动词。

entries.definition: the continuous act of checking or watching something. It is the process, while monitor is the device or the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查或观察的行为。它是过程，而 monitor 是设备或动词。

entries.definition: giving or serving as a warning. It keeps the Latin sense of admonition and is mostly formal.
entries.definitionCN: 给予警告的，或起警告作用的。它保留了拉丁语“告诫”的意思，多用于正式语境。

entries.definition: to warn or reprimand someone firmly but not harshly. It shares the Latin monere root but is a separate verb, not a form of monitor.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定但不严厉地警告或责备某人。它与 monitor 共享拉丁语 monere 词根，但它是另一个动词，不是 monitor 的词形。

entries.definition: a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something bad. It is a warning that comes before the event, built with pre- 'before'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种某事即将发生、尤指坏事的感觉。它是事件之前到来的警告，由 pre-“在前”构成。

entries.definition: to be in charge of people or work and make sure it is done properly. It stresses authority over workers, while monitor stresses continuous checking of signals or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 负责管理人或工作，确保事情做好。它强调对工作者的权威，而 monitor 强调对信号或状况的持续检查。

entries.definition: to look at something for a period of time, often without measuring it. Monitor usually adds a purpose: to detect change, risk, or poor quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内看着某物，通常不进行测量。monitor 通常多一层目的：发现变化、风险或质量问题。

entries.definition: to follow the movement or development of something over time, often by recorded traces. It focuses on where something goes; monitor focuses on whether it stays within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间跟踪某物的移动或发展，常依据记录下来的痕迹。它关注东西去了哪里，monitor 关注它是否仍在限度之内。

entries.definition: to examine people, substances, or signals in order to sort or filter them. It is usually a test applied at a point in time, while monitor is a watch kept over time.
entries.definitionCN: 检查人、物质或信号，以便分类或筛选。它通常是在某一时点施行的检验，而 monitor 是长期保持的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin monere 'warn', the agent noun monitor, and the English family monitoring, monitory, admonish, and premonition.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 monere“警告”、施动名词 monitor，以及英语词族 monitoring、monitory、admonish、premonition。

normal.en: monere means 'to warn, remind'. A monitor is literally 'one who warns' — first a pupil, then an instrument, then a screen.
normal.cn: monere 意为“警告、提醒”。monitor 字面上就是“发出警告的人”——先是学生，再是仪器，最后是屏幕。

normal.en: The school sense is the oldest English one (1540s); the machine and screen senses are centuries later.
normal.cn: 学校职务义是英语里最古老的义项（16 世纪 40 年代）；仪器与屏幕义要晚好几个世纪。

normal.en: The verb arrived in 1924 for checking radio signal quality, which is why 'monitor a channel' still sounds natural.
normal.cn: 动词于 1924 年出现，用于检查无线电信号质量，所以 monitor a channel 至今听起来自然。

normal.en: monitoring is the process, monitory is 'warning', admonish is a separate verb from the same root.
normal.cn: monitoring 是过程，monitory 是“警告的”，admonish 则是同根的另一动词。

normal.en: A monitor differs from a supervisor: it keeps checking a signal or condition, while a supervisor holds authority over people.
normal.cn: monitor 与 supervisor 不同：它持续检查信号或状况，而 supervisor 对人拥有管理权。

abstract.en: Picture a night watchman at a factory gate. He does not repair anything; he looks, checks, and raises the alarm.
abstract.cn: 想象一名守在工厂大门的更夫。他不修理任何东西；他看、检查、发出警报。

abstract.en: Move that watchman into a box on the wall, and he becomes a heart monitor; put his gaze on a screen, and he becomes a display.
abstract.cn: 把这位更夫装进墙上的盒子，他就成了心脏监测仪；把他的目光放到屏幕上，他就成了显示器。

abstract.en: The word always means attention spread over time: a single look is not monitoring, however careful it is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终表示铺在时间上的注意：只看一眼，无论多仔细，都不算监测。

examples.en: Nurses monitor the patient's pulse and blood pressure every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时监测病人的脉搏与血压。

examples.en: The app monitors how much time you spend on each website.
examples.cn: 这个应用监控你在每个网站上花多少时间。

examples.en: The teacher left a monitor in charge of the class while she fetched the keys.
examples.cn: 老师去取钥匙时，让班长负责管班。

dict_mnemonic.text: “莫离他”——莫要离开他，他一直在旁边盯着、随时提醒你 → monitor 监视器；监测（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 monere“警告、提醒”的施动名词 monitor“告诫者”，核心是“持续盯着并随时发出提醒”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of monitor, all held together by one figure: someone standing beside a thing, watching without stopping and speaking up when something is wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: monitor 的十个义项都由同一个形象串起：有人站在某物旁边，不停地看，一有不对就出声提醒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warner standing beside, eyes fixed on one spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站在旁边、目光钉在一处的告诫者。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: the warner becomes a measuring device, and the screen that shows its check takes the same name.
branches.cn: 仪器：告诫者变成测量设备，显示这项检查的屏幕也沿用了同一个名字。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the oldest senses keep a person in the role, either a pupil keeping order or an official who warns.
branches.cn: 人：最古老的义项让一个人留在这个角色里，或是维持秩序的学生，或是提出告诫的官员。

branches.en: WATCHING: the verb checks quantities over time, and when aimed at people it becomes surveillance.
branches.cn: 注视：动词随时间检查数量，而当对象转向人时，它就变成监控。

branches.en: LISTENING: a channel is watched with the ears, the earliest verb use of all.
branches.cn: 监听：频道是用耳朵看的，这是所有动词用法中最早的一个。

branches.en: THE NAME TRAVELS: a lizard fabled to warn, an ironclad built to admonish, and a background program that keeps checking.
branches.cn: 名字远行：传说会预警的蜥蜴、为告诫而造的铁甲舰，以及持续检查的后台程序。

intro.en: Monitor is a Latin agent noun in -itor built on mon- 'warn'. English adds -ing, -y, -ial and -ship, while the same root also reaches English through admonish, monition, and premonition.
intro.cn: monitor 是拉丁语中以 -itor 结尾的施动名词，词干 mon- 意为“警告”。英语加上 -ing、-y、-ial 与 -ship，同一词根还通过 admonish、monition、premonition 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is monere 'warn, remind', its agent noun monitor, and the action noun monitio 'a warning'. Summon also belongs here: Latin summonere meant 'hint, remind, warn'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词族包括 monere“警告、提醒”、它的施动名词 monitor，以及行为名词 monitio“警告”。summon 也属于这里：拉丁语 summonere 意为“暗示、提醒、警告”。

items.meaning: one who warns or checks; a checking device
items.meaningCN: 告诫者；检查者；监测设备（mon- 警告 + -itor 施动名词）
items.example: The monitor on the wall showed a steady line.
items.exampleCN: 墙上的监测仪显示出一条平稳的线。

items.meaningCN: 监测；监控（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: The patient was kept under close monitoring.
items.exampleCN: 病人被置于密切监测之下。

items.meaningCN: 告诫的；警告的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave a monitory glance at the noisy table.
items.exampleCN: 他朝吵闹的那桌投去一个警告的目光。

items.meaning: relating to a monitor or prefect
items.meaningCN: 级长的；监督的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The monitorial duties rotated each week.

items.meaningCN: 告诫；温和地责备（ad- 向 + mon- 警告）
items.example: The coach admonished the players for arriving late.
items.exampleCN: 教练因球员迟到而告诫了他们。

items.example: She ignored the admonition and drove faster.
items.exampleCN: 她无视那句告诫，反而开得更快。

items.meaning: a warning, especially an official one
items.meaningCN: 警告；正式告诫（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The court issued a monition to the landowner.
items.exampleCN: 法院向那位土地所有者发出正式警告。

items.meaning: a feeling that something is coming
items.meaningCN: 预感；事前警告（pre- 在前 + monition 警告）
items.example: She had a premonition that the flight would be delayed.
items.exampleCN: 她预感到那趟航班会延误。

items.meaningCN: 召唤；传唤（sum- 暗中 + mon- 提醒）
items.example: The manager summoned the clerk to her office.
items.exampleCN: 经理把那名职员叫到办公室。

items.structure: Greek Mentor, perhaps from PIE *men- 'to think'
items.meaningCN: 导师；可信赖的顾问（同出“思考”词根）
items.example: She became a mentor to the younger researchers.
items.exampleCN: 她成了年轻研究者的导师。

definition_zh: 月；月份；一个月的时间；漫长的岁月（复数）
definition_en: one of the twelve divisions of the year, also a period of about thirty days and, in the plural, a long stretch of time
core_image: 日历上撕下的一页，边缘还留着月亮的弧度
scene: 月底的夜里，桌上的账单摊开，日期一格一格逼近。The rent falls due at the start of every month.
sceneCN: 这里是「月份、月」（第 1 个义项：日历上的一年十二分之一）；句意为每到月初房租就到期。图中可辨识物件：账单、日历、台灯。

pos.zh: 月；月份；一个月的时间；漫长的岁月

derivatives.zh: 由 month 加 -ly 构成，义为「每月的；每月一次」
由 month 与 long 复合而成，义为「持续一个月的」
由前缀 bi-（两个）加 monthly 构成，义为「两月一次的」

senses.title: One of the twelve divisions of the year
senses.definition: one of the twelve named divisions of the calendar year
senses.definitionCN: 日历年里十二个有名称的划分之一
senses.example: February is the shortest month of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 二月是一年里最短的月份。
senses.why: A month began as the moon's own cycle, so the word for the unit still carries the shape of a turning moon.
senses.whyCN: 月份最初就是月亮自己的一轮周期，所以这个表单位的词里仍留着月亮转动的形状。

senses.title: A period of about thirty days
senses.definition: a span of roughly thirty days used as a unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 用作计时单位的大约三十天的一段时间
senses.example: The repairs took a month to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工作花了一个月才完成。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, it can measure any span of about thirty days, whether or not the calendar page matches.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，它就能用来量任何约三十天的时间段，不必与日历那一页严格对齐。

senses.title: A long stretch of time, in the plural
senses.definition: a long time, used in the plural to suggest a slow wait
senses.definitionCN: 很长的一段时间，用复数来表示漫长的等待
senses.example: She has not written to us for months.
senses.exampleCN: 她好几个月没有给我们写信了。
senses.why: Counting months is slow, so a plural pile of them naturally stands for a long wait.
senses.whyCN: 按月计数本来就慢，于是复数的月份自然就表示一段漫长的等待。

senses.title: The lunar cycle
senses.definition: the period from one new moon to the next, about twenty-nine and a half days
senses.definitionCN: 从一个新月到下一个新月的周期，约二十九天半
senses.example: A lunar month lasts about twenty-nine and a half days.
senses.exampleCN: 一个太阴月约持续二十九天半。
senses.why: The moon-based origin keeps a technical sense alive in astronomy, where a lunar month runs from one new moon to the next.
senses.whyCN: 以月亮为起点的来源让一个术语义在天文学里保留下来：太阴月从一个新月走到下一个新月。

intro.en: The English month is a Germanic word built on the moon, and its oldest sense is a moon-driven cycle rather than a page on a wall.
intro.cn: 英语的 month 是建立在月亮之上的日耳曼词，它最早的意思是被月亮推动的一轮周期，而不是墙上的一页纸。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to measure is generally thought to lie behind the words for moon and month in both the Germanic and the Latin branches.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个表示「测量」的印欧语重构词根同时藏在日耳曼语和拉丁语中表示月亮与月份的词后面。

items.en: Old English mōnaþ joined mōna, the moon, with the noun suffix -þ, so the month was literally the moon's turning.
items.cn: 古英语 mōnaþ 把 mōna（月亮）与名词后缀 -þ 结合，所以月份字面上就是月亮的一轮转动。

items.en: Related forms such as Old Frisian mōnath and German Monat show the same moon-based naming across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古弗里斯兰语的 mōnath、德语的 Monat 等相关形式显示，日耳曼各语言都用月亮来命名月份。

items.en: Middle English moneth kept the moon inside the word while the spelling slowly moved toward the modern month.
items.cn: 中古英语的 moneth 仍把月亮留在词里，拼写则慢慢向现代形式 month 靠拢。

items.en: Modern English month covers the calendar unit, the lunar cycle and, in the plural, a long stretch of time.
items.cn: 现代英语的 month 兼指日历单位、月相周期，复数还表示很长一段时间。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same moon stem, while the near-meaning group collects the other units used to count time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一月亮词干上的形式，近义组收用来计时的其他单位。

entries.definition: Happening once every month or issued each month.
entries.definitionCN: 由 month 加 -ly 构成，义为「每月的；每月一次」。

entries.definition: The body whose cycle gave the month its name.
entries.definitionCN: 其周期为月份提供名称的天体，月亮。

entries.definition: The day named after the moon, from the same Old English stem.
entries.definitionCN: 以月亮命名的日子，来自同一个古英语词干。

entries.definition: A period of seven days, the unit just below a month.
entries.definitionCN: 七天的一段时间，是比月更小的计时单位。

entries.definition: A period of twelve months.
entries.definitionCN: 十二个月的一段时间。

entries.definition: A period of two weeks, common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 两周的一段时间，英式用法中常见。

entries.definition: A period of twenty-four hours.
entries.definitionCN: 二十四小时的一段时间。

normalIntro.en: The word is a moon-word from start to finish, and its family keeps returning to cycling light and counted time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都是月亮词，它的同族词也一直回到光的循环与被数出来的时间。

normal.en: Old English mōnaþ is moon plus a noun ending, so the month was named after the moon that paced it.
normal.cn: 古英语 mōnaþ 是月亮加一个名词词尾，月份是用给它定节奏的月亮命名的。

normal.en: German Monat and Dutch maand keep the same m-n shape, which is why the English word looks so plain.
normal.cn: 德语 Monat 与荷兰语 maand 保留同样的 m-n 骨架，所以英语这个词显得格外朴素。

normal.en: monthly adds -ly to month: something that happens once in each month.
normal.cn: monthly 在 month 后加 -ly，表示在每个月发生一次的事物。

normal.en: The plural months often means a long time, as in letters unanswered for months.
normal.cn: 复数的 months 常表示很久，例如好几个月没有回信。

normal.en: Latin mensis is a distant cousin rather than a borrowing, which is why English did not take a Latin shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mensis 是远亲而不是借词，所以英语没有采用拉丁语的词形。

abstract.en: A calendar is a row of moons, each one handing its name to a page.
abstract.cn: 日历就是一排月亮，每一个把自己的名字交给一页纸。

abstract.en: Turn a page and a moon has already happened.
abstract.cn: 翻过一页，就有一轮月亮已经走完。

abstract.en: The word is older than paper: people counted months by looking up.
abstract.cn: 这个词比纸更老：人们曾靠抬头看天来数月份。

examples.en: February is the shortest month of the year.
examples.cn: 二月是一年里最短的月份。

examples.en: The repairs took a month to finish.
examples.cn: 修理工作花了一个月才完成。

examples.en: She has not written to us for months.
examples.cn: 她好几个月没有给我们写信了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「忙死」——月底事情多到忙死；记住 month 就是月。

root: 古英语 mōnaþ 由 mōna（月亮）加名词后缀 -þ 构成，本义是月亮的一轮；一般认为它与拉丁语 mensis 同出印欧语表示「测量」的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the calendar unit, and the senses then branch into a measured span, a slow plural of waiting, and the lunar cycle underneath it all.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是日历上的月份；义项由此分出被丈量的时间段、表示漫长等待的复数，以及藏在底下的月相周期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page torn from a calendar, its edge still curved like a moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从日历上撕下的纸，边缘仍带着月牙的弧度。

branches.en: a calendar page torn off on the first day
branches.cn: 月初撕下的一页日历

branches.en: a repair job stretching across thirty days
branches.cn: 一项横跨三十天的修理活

branches.en: letters left unanswered for a season
branches.cn: 一整个季节无人回的信

branches.en: a chart tracing new moon to new moon
branches.cn: 从新月画到新月的图

branches.en: rent falling due as a month turns
branches.cn: 月份交替时到期的房租

intro.en: The word is held together by a moon noun, an old noun ending, and the two suffixes that turn it into a monthly adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示月亮的名词、一个古老的名词词尾，以及把它变成「每月的」形容词的两个后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin mensis and menstruus belong to the same distant Indo-European family, though English borrowed nothing directly from them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mensis 与 menstruus 属于同一遥远的印欧语族，但英语并没有直接借用它们。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词与副词的后缀

items.meaning: the body that paces the month

items.meaningCN: 由 moon 与 day 复合

definition_zh: 月亮；月球；卫星；（诗）月光；（动词）闲荡、出神；（英俚）露出臀部
definition_en: the natural body that orbits the earth, or any natural satellite of a planet
core_image: 院墙上方一轮圆月升到屋脊那么高，瓦片被照出淡蓝色的光
scene: 院墙上方，一轮圆月升到屋脊那么高，瓦片被照出淡蓝的光。Above the courtyard wall, the moon has risen level with the roof tiles.
sceneCN: 这里 moon 指「绕地球运行的天然卫星，即月球」（第 1 个义项：地球的天然卫星）；句意为院墙上方，月亮已升到与屋瓦齐高。图中可辨识物件：院墙、圆月、屋脊、瓦片、淡蓝月色；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 闲荡、出神；（英俚）露出臀部

derivatives.zh: 卫星（复数）
月光照亮的
月光
小卫星
月球的

senses.title: The earth's natural satellite
senses.definition: the body that orbits the earth and causes tides and eclipses
senses.definitionCN: 绕地球运行、引起潮汐与食象的天体
senses.example: Above the courtyard wall, the moon has risen level with the roof tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 院墙上方，月亮已升到与屋瓦齐高。
senses.why: the word is native English, not borrowed, because the moon is the one sky object everyone could name without astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语本族词而非借词，因为月亮是无需天文学人人都会命名的天体。

senses.title: Its visible shape and phases
senses.definition: the moon as seen from earth, changing shape through the month
senses.definitionCN: 从地球所见的月亮，其形状在一个月里变化
senses.example: A thin crescent moon hung just above the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 一弯细细的月牙挂在山丘上方。
senses.why: what people call 'the moon' is usually the lit part they can see, so the word names an appearance as well as a body.
senses.whyCN: 人们所说的「月亮」通常指能看见的那部分亮面，因此这个词既指天体也指外观。

senses.title: Any planet's moon
senses.definition: a natural satellite of any planet, not only the earth's
senses.definitionCN: 任何行星的天然卫星，不限于地球的
senses.example: Jupiter's moons were the first found beyond our own.
senses.exampleCN: 木星的卫星是最早在我们月球之外被发现的。
senses.why: once Galileo saw four points circling Jupiter, the common noun extended from one moon to many.
senses.whyCN: 当伽利略看到四个光点绕木星后，这个普通名词便从一个月亮扩展到许多个。

senses.title: Moonlight
senses.definition: the light reflected from the moon, especially in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 月球反射的光，尤用于文学语言
senses.example: They walked home by the light of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借着月光走回家。
senses.why: since the moon's light is its most noticeable effect on earth, the noun easily stands for the light itself.
senses.whyCN: 月之光是对地球最显著的影响，因此这个名词很容易代指光本身。

senses.title: Many moons ago
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase many moons ago, meaning a long time in the past
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语「许多个月亮以前」，意为很久以前
senses.example: Many moons ago this field was an orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，这片地是一座果园。
senses.why: a moon also meant a month, so counting moons was counting months, and the phrase keeps that older reckoning.
senses.whyCN: moon 也曾指一个月，因此数月亮就是数月份，这个短语保留了这种古老算法。

senses.title: To moon about
senses.definition: to spend time aimlessly or dreamily, as in mooning around the house
senses.definitionCN: 无所事事或恍恍惚惚地消磨时间，如在家里闲荡
senses.example: He mooned about the garden all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个下午都在花园里闲荡。
senses.why: the verb pictures someone drifting like a moon across the sky, with no fixed direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把人想成像月亮一样在天上漂移，没有固定方向。

senses.title: British slang: to moon
senses.definition: in informal British use, to show one's bare buttocks as a joke or insult
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中，为玩笑或羞辱而露出光屁股
senses.example: The comedian mooned the crowd and was booed.
senses.exampleCN: 那个喜剧演员对观众露臀，被喝了倒彩。
senses.why: the slang sense plays on a pale round shape, but it is a separate development and should not be confused with the astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个俚语义借的是苍白圆形的样子，但它是独立发展出来的，不应与天文学义混淆。

senses.title: A lunar month
senses.definition: the period of the moon's cycle, about twenty-nine and a half days, once used to measure months
senses.definitionCN: 月亮盈亏一周的时长，约二十九天半，曾用来计量月份
senses.example: The festival follows the moon rather than the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日按月亮而非太阳计算。
senses.why: month and moon come from the same root, so the calendar still carries the moon's cycle inside it.
senses.whyCN: month 与 moon 同出一根，因此历法里仍装着月亮的周期。

senses.title: Promise the moon
senses.definition: in idioms such as promise the moon, to offer something impossible
senses.definitionCN: 在「许诺月亮」等习语中，指许下不可能兑现的事
senses.example: Politicians promise the moon and deliver a lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 政客许诺月亮，却只送来一盏灯。
senses.why: the moon is visibly out of reach, which makes it the natural object for a promise no one can keep.
senses.whyCN: 月亮显然够不着，因此它自然成了无人能兑现的承诺的对象。

intro.en: Moon is native English, from Old English mōna, from Proto-Germanic *mēnô and a reconstructed Indo-European stem for 'moon, month'. It is not related to Latin luna. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: moon 是英语本族词，来自古英语 mōna、原始日耳曼语 *mēnô，再往前是表示「月亮、月份」的印欧词干重构形式。它与拉丁 luna 没有直接关系。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English mōna named the moon and also stood for a month, a link still visible in month and Monday.
items.cn: 古英语 mōna 指月亮，也指一个月；这一联系仍见于 month 与 Monday。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic form *mēnô is reconstructed from the Germanic languages; no written record of it survives.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语形式 *mēnô 由各日耳曼语言重构而来，没有书面记录留存。

items.en: The stem usually written *mḗh₁n̥s meant both 'moon' and 'month' and is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 通常写作 *mḗh₁n̥s 的词干兼指「月亮」与「月份」，属重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: The same root idea connects the moon to measuring time, which is why month, Monday and 'many moons' all belong here.
items.cn: 同一词根把月亮与计时联系起来，因此 month、Monday 与「many moons」都属此处。

items.en: Latin luna 'moon' comes from a different root connected with light, and gives lunar, not moon.
items.cn: 拉丁 luna「月亮」来自另一个与光有关的词根，派生的是 lunar，而非 moon。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the exact Indo-European shape and its relation to the 'measure' root are debated, so the form given here is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：确切的印欧形态及其与「测量」词根的关系仍有争议，此处给出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same native stem; group two holds sky words that overlap in use.
note.cn: 第一组是同出本族词干的词；第二组是用法重叠的天空词。

entries.definition: A unit of the calendar, from the same root as moon; it names time, not the body.
entries.definitionCN: 历法单位，与 moon 同根；命名时间，而非天体。

entries.definition: Literally 'moon's day', a calque of Latin dies lunae; it keeps the older religious naming.
entries.definitionCN: 字面「月亮之日」，仿译拉丁 dies lunae；保留了更古老的宗教命名。

entries.definition: The light reflected by the moon; a compound, not a second object.
entries.definitionCN: 月球反射的光；是复合词，不指第二个天体。

entries.definition: A very small natural satellite; the -let suffix marks size, not kind.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的天然卫星；-let 后缀标记大小，而非种类。

entries.definition: The general word for any orbiting body, natural or artificial; moon is the everyday and native word.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何绕行天体，天然或人造；moon 是日常的本族词。

entries.definition: The curved shape of a waxing or waning moon; it names a phase, not the body.
entries.definitionCN: 盈缺月牙的弯曲形状；命名月相，而非天体。

entries.definition: The Latin-derived adjective for the moon; it replaces 'of the moon' in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 源自拉丁的月球形容词；在技术文字中替代「月亮的」。

entries.definition: An old word for a heavenly light, especially sun or moon; it treats the moon as a lamp.
entries.definitionCN: 指天空发光体的旧词，尤指日月；把月亮当作一盏灯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relatives, real compounds and real idioms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实同族词、真实搭配与真实习语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: moon and month share one root: a moon was a way of counting time.
normal.cn: moon 与 month 同根：月亮曾是计时方式。

normal.en: Monday is literally the moon's day.
normal.cn: Monday 字面就是「月亮之日」。

normal.en: The family runs moon, moons, moonlight, moonlit, moonlet, lunar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 moon、moons、moonlight、moonlit、moonlet、lunar。

normal.en: Phases are fixed phrases: full moon, new moon, crescent moon, moon phase.
normal.cn: 月相是固定搭配：满月、新月、月牙、月相。

normal.en: Two idioms mark the word: many moons ago, once in a blue moon.
normal.cn: 两个习语标记这个词：很久以前、千载难逢。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that changes its shape every night but never moves its post.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯每晚换形状，却从不挪动位置。

abstract.en: Picture a coin that is sometimes a thin edge and sometimes a full face.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币，有时只见薄边，有时见整面。

abstract.en: Picture a promise written on something nobody can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象把承诺写在一个谁也够不着的东西上。

examples.en: The moon rises about fifty minutes later each night.
examples.cn: 月亮每晚大约晚五十分钟升起。

examples.en: Saturn has more moons than any other planet.
examples.cn: 土星的卫星比任何其他行星都多。

examples.en: They met once in a blue moon, usually by the river.
examples.cn: 他们难得见一面，通常在河边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「木嗯（moon）」——夜里抬头「嗯」一声看见的那轮圆盘 → 月亮

root: 古英语 mōna ← 原始日耳曼语 *mēnô ← 印欧词干 *mḗh₁n̥s（兼指月亮与月份，属重构形式）；与拉丁 luna 不同源，luna 另出与光有关的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one object but change the angle: the body, its visible phase, other planets' moons, its light, its use as a month, two verbs, a calendar cycle and an impossible promise.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守着同一个天体，却不断换角度：天体、可见月相、别行星的卫星、它的光、它当月份、两个动词义、历法周期，以及一个够不着的承诺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round pale light above a wall, changing shape but staying in the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上方一轮淡色圆光，形状会变，却始终在天上。

branches.en: OBJECT AND LOOK: the same word names the body and the shape people see.
branches.cn: 天体与外观：同一个词既指天体，也指人们看见的形状。

branches.en: FROM ONE TO MANY: Galileo's four points made moon a countable class.
branches.cn: 从一到多：伽利略看到的四个光点使 moon 成为可数类别。

branches.en: LIGHT AND TIME: the moon gives light and once gave the month.
branches.cn: 光与时间：月亮给光，也曾给月份。

branches.en: IDIOMATIC REACH: counting moons measures the past, and promising one measures impossibility.
branches.cn: 习语中的尺度：数月亮量过去，许月亮量不可能。

branches.en: VERBAL DRIFT: drifting like a moon, and a slang joke on its pale round shape.
branches.cn: 动词漂移：像月亮一样漂，以及拿它苍白圆形开的俚语玩笑。

intro.en: Moon is a single native English root; its family is built by compounding and by the small suffix -let, not by Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: moon 是单一的英语本族词根；其词族靠复合与小型后缀 -let 构成，不用拉丁前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin used luna for the moon, a different root; English technical adjectives come from it, while the noun itself stays native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 luna 指月亮，属另一词根；英语技术形容词由它而来，而名词本身仍是本族词。

items.example: The moon rose over the wall.

他们穿过月光下的田野。

items.example: A moonlet orbits inside the ring.
items.exampleCN: 一颗小卫星在环内运行。

items.example: The moon landing was watched worldwide.
The month follows the moon's cycle.
Monday is named for the moon.

definition_zh: 早晨；上午；黎明；开端
definition_en: the early part of the day from sunrise to noon, also dawn itself and the opening phase of something
core_image: 窗帘缝里透进来的第一道光
scene: 天还没亮，海面上只剩雾和远处一盏航标灯。By morning the fog had lifted off the harbour.
sceneCN: 这里是「早晨、上午」（第 1 个义项：天亮到中午前的一段时间）；句意为到天亮时雾已从港口散去。图中可辨识物件：海雾、航标灯、码头。

derivatives.zh: 去掉词尾 -ing 得到的书面短形式，义为「晨」
同一词干保留较早含义，义为「次日」
由 morning 与 glory 复合，指清晨开放的牵牛花

senses.title: The early part of the day
senses.definition: the time from sunrise until noon
senses.definitionCN: 从日出到中午的一段时间
senses.example: The market opens early in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 市场在清晨就开门了。
senses.why: The Germanic word named the hours when light returns, and English kept that plain, everyday sense as the core.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼词本来指光回来的那段时间，英语把这个朴素的日常含义保留为核心。

senses.title: Dawn itself
senses.definition: the moment when the sky first grows light
senses.definitionCN: 天空开始变亮的那一刻
senses.example: Morning came slowly over the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 曙色慢慢越过群山。
senses.why: Because the word first meant the turning of the night, it can name the single moment of first light rather than the whole morning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指夜色转折的那一刻，所以它能指第一道光的瞬间，而不只是整个上午。

senses.title: The opening phase of something
senses.definition: the early stage of a period, thought of as its dawn
senses.definitionCN: 一个时期的早期阶段，被看作它的黎明
senses.example: The morning of the industry was full of wild experiments.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业的初期充满了大胆的试验。
senses.why: If a day begins with a morning, any period can be given a morning, so the word becomes a metaphor for beginnings.
senses.whyCN: 一天以早晨开场，任何时期也就可以有一个早晨，于是这个词成了开端的比喻。

senses.title: A morning greeting
senses.definition: used in the greeting good morning
senses.definitionCN: 用于问候语 good morning 之中
senses.example: He called out a cheerful good morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他高声说了一句爽朗的早上好。
senses.why: A greeting names the time it belongs to, so morning became part of a fixed social formula.
senses.whyCN: 问候语会用它所属的时间来命名，于是早晨就成了一个固定社交用语的一部分。

intro.en: The word began as a Germanic name for the light-returning hours and gained its ending in Middle English by analogy with the word for evening.
intro.cn: 这个词最初是日耳曼语中对光线回归时段的称呼，在中古英语里仿照表示傍晚的词补上了词尾。

items.en: A reconstructed form generally taken as murganaz is the common Germanic ancestor of the words for morning.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构形式 murganaz 是日耳曼各语言中表示早晨的词的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English morgen meant morning and could also point to the next day, a sense that survives in morrow.
items.cn: 古英语 morgen 意为早晨，也能指次日，这个含义仍留在 morrow 里。

items.en: Middle English added the ending -ing to morwen, producing morweninge, perhaps by analogy with evening.
items.cn: 中古英语在 morwen 后加上词尾 -ing，形成 morweninge，这也许是仿照 evening 的结果。

items.en: By the early modern period the form had shortened to morning and the greeting good morning was fixed.
items.cn: 到近代早期，这个词形已缩短为 morning，问候语 good morning 也固定下来。

items.en: Modern English morning names the early hours and, figuratively, the opening phase of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语的 morning 指清早的几个小时，也比喻任何事物的开端阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the same old stem or built with the same ending, while the near-meaning group collects the words for first light.
note.cn: 形近组收同一古老词干上的形式或用了相同词尾的形式，近义组收表示初光的词。

entries.definition: A literary shortening of morning.
entries.definitionCN: morning 的书面缩短形式。

entries.definition: The next day, from the older sense of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 次日，来自同一词干的较早含义。

entries.definition: The matching time word for the end of the day, built with a similar ending but a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 与早晨相对的一天尾声用词，结尾形式相似但词根不同。

entries.definition: The first light of day.
entries.definitionCN: 一天中的第一道光。

entries.definition: The part of the day before noon, a formal word.
entries.definitionCN: 中午之前的那段时间，较书面。

entries.definition: The moment when daylight begins.
entries.definitionCN: 天亮的那一刻。

normalIntro.en: The word grew from a Germanic name for the returning light, and its family keeps the sense of a day turning over.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从日耳曼语中表示光线回归的名称长出来，同族词都保留着一天翻页的感觉。

normal.en: Old English morgen is the base, and Middle English added -ing, much as evening was formed.
normal.cn: 古英语 morgen 是底子，中古英语加上 -ing，很像 evening 的构成方式。

normal.en: morrow, meaning the next day, keeps the older sense of morgen as tomorrow.
normal.cn: morrow 意为次日，保留了 morgen 指明天的较早含义。

normal.en: Good morning is a fixed greeting, so the word also names a social ritual.
normal.cn: good morning 是固定问候语，所以这个词也指一种社交礼节。

normal.en: The plural mornings appears in phrases like early mornings, naming repeated occasions.
normal.cn: 复数的 mornings 出现在 early mornings 一类短语里，指反复出现的清晨。

normal.en: morning-glory is a compound: a flower that opens with the day.
normal.cn: morning-glory 是复合词，指随白天开放的花。

abstract.en: Morning is the word for light returning to the same room.
abstract.cn: 早晨就是光回到同一间屋子的那个词。

abstract.en: Every morning is a page with nothing written on it yet.
abstract.cn: 每个早晨都是一张还没写上字的纸。

abstract.en: The word carries both a clock and a beginning, which is why a career can have a morning.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装着钟点和开端，所以一段事业也可以有它的早晨。

examples.en: The market opens early in the morning.
examples.cn: 市场在清晨就开门了。

examples.en: Morning came slowly over the hills.
examples.cn: 曙色慢慢越过群山。

examples.en: He called out a cheerful good morning.
examples.cn: 他高声说了一句爽朗的早上好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸宁」——摸黑等到天亮，四周变宁；记住 morning 是早晨。

root: 中古英语 morweninge 由 morwen（早晨，源自古英语 morgen）加 -ing 构成，一般认为模仿了 evening 的形式。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the early hours; the senses then divide into first light, the opening phase of anything, and the fixed greeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是清早的时段；义项由此分出第一道光、万事万物的开端阶段，以及固定问候语中的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first beam slipping through a gap in the curtains onto the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一道光从窗帘缝隙里滑进来，落在地板上。

branches.en: a kitchen lit before the street wakes
branches.cn: 街上还没醒，厨房先亮了

branches.en: first light touching the water
branches.cn: 初光落在水面上

branches.en: the first years of a movement
branches.cn: 一场运动的头几年

branches.en: a greeting exchanged at the gate
branches.cn: 在门口交换的一句问候

branches.en: fog lifting as the day turns
branches.cn: 天翻页时散去的雾

intro.en: The word joins an old Germanic noun for morning with a noun ending shared by other time words, and it still splits into short and compound forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把日耳曼语中表示早晨的古名词与一个和其他时间词共用的名词词尾接在一起，并且还分出缩短形式与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，因此拉丁语部分留空。

a flower that opens at dawn

definition_zh: 主要地；大部分；通常；几乎全部
definition_en: for the greatest part of a group or amount; in most cases or most of the time; and almost entirely
core_image: 一只盘子里大半装着米饭，边角只留几样小菜
scene: 傍晚的自助餐厅里，长桌大半已经空了，只有靠窗那几盘菜还被夹得七零八落。By eight the buffet was quiet, and the trays that were mostly empty had been stacked by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「大半、大部分」（第 1 个义项：指一个整体中的多数部分）；句意为到八点时自助餐区已经安静下来，那些大半空了的托盘被叠在门边。图中可辨识物件：长餐台、成摞的托盘、靠窗的菜盘。

pos.zh: 主要地；大部分；通常；几乎全部

derivatives.zh: 与 mostly 同源的基础词，去掉副词后缀 -ly 即得，义为「最多的；大多数的」
由古英语 eall（全部）与 māst（最多）缩合而成，义为「几乎」，与 most 同源
由古英语 ūt（向外）加 most 构成，义为「最远的；极度的」

senses.title: The greatest share of a group
senses.definition: applying to the greater number of people or things in a group
senses.definitionCN: 适用于一个群体中数量占多数的人或物
senses.example: The guests at the wedding were mostly relatives from her side.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼上的宾客多半是她这边的亲戚。
senses.why: The word is built on the Old English superlative māst, the greatest share, so its first duty is to report how a whole divides rather than to name a frequency.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在古英语最高级 māst（最大的份额）上，所以它首先管的是「一个整体怎么分」，而不是说事情多久发生一次。

senses.title: In most cases, as a habit
senses.definition: happening on most occasions, though not on every one
senses.definitionCN: 在多数场合都会发生，但并非每一次
senses.example: He mostly takes the early train and reads on the way.
senses.exampleCN: 他通常坐早班车，在路上看书。
senses.why: Once the word could mark the larger part of anything, it could also mark the larger part of a routine, which is how a share of a group turned into a habitual frequency.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能标出任何事物里较大的那部分，它也就能标出日常习惯里较大的那部分，群体份额就这样长成了习惯性的频率。

senses.title: Nearly the whole of an amount
senses.definition: covering the largest part of a quantity or substance, with only a small remainder
senses.definitionCN: 占去数量或物质的最大部分，只剩下很少一点
senses.example: The bottle in the shed is mostly rainwater.
senses.exampleCN: 棚子里那瓶装的几乎全是雨水。
senses.why: Measuring a substance leaves a visible remainder, so the same superlative sense reads as a near total: the greatest share of a bottle is almost the bottle, and the rest is an exception.
senses.whyCN: 给一样东西计量时总会剩下一小点，于是同一个最高级的意思读成了「接近全部」：一只瓶子里的最大份额就是几乎整瓶，剩下那点只是例外。

intro.en: Mostly is an Old English superlative turned into an adverb: most, the greatest share, plus the ending -ly, which says in what manner a statement holds.
intro.cn: mostly 是古英语最高级加副词词尾构成的词：most 指最大的份额，-ly 表示一句话以什么方式成立。

items.en: Māst was the superlative of micel, great, and it named the greatest amount or the greatest share of a group.
items.cn: māst 是 micel（大的）的最高级，指最大的数量，或一个群体中最大的份额。

items.en: The ending -līce came from līc, body or form, and it turned an adjective into an adverb meaning in the manner of something; in English it settled as -ly.
items.cn: -līce 这个词尾出自 līc（身体、形貌），把形容词变成表示「以……方式」的副词；进入英语后固定为 -ly。

items.en: Middle English joined most and -ly into mostli, an adverb reporting what holds for the greater number of cases.
items.cn: 中古英语把 most 与 -ly 合成 mostli，用作副词，表示对多数情形都成立。

items.en: By the fifteenth century mostly was common in the sense of for the greatest part, and it stood beside almost, which had grown from all and most.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，mostly 已常见，意为「大部分」；它与由 all 与 most 合成的 almost 并列使用。

items.en: Modern English keeps three readings: a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount, and dictionaries list them as separate senses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三种读法：群体中的份额、习惯性的频率、数量上接近全部；词典把它们分列为不同义项。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Old English words that share the most element; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of majority and frequency.
note.cn: 形近组收与 most 共用词素的古英语词与英语词；近义组收表示多数与频率的副词。

entries.definition: The greatest amount, or the greater number of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 最大的数量，或一个群体中的多数。

entries.definition: Not quite, but very nearly.
entries.definitionCN: 差一点，但非常接近。

entries.definition: Farthest out, or greatest in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 最远的，或程度最大的。

entries.definition: Ranking first in importance or position.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或位置上居首的。

entries.definition: More than anything else, or for the greater part.
entries.definitionCN: 首要地，或大部分情况下。

entries.definition: To a great extent.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上。

entries.definition: In most cases or on most occasions.
entries.definitionCN: 多数情况下，或多数场合。

entries.definition: Above all; mostly but not only.
entries.definitionCN: 首先；主要是，但不只是。

normalIntro.en: The word is one Old English superlative plus one adverbial ending, and everything about it follows from the idea of the greatest share.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一个古英语最高级加一个副词词尾，它的全部用法都从「最大份额」这个想法里长出来。

normal.en: Most is the superlative of great, so mostly begins with the idea of the greatest share, not with a vague idea of many.
normal.cn: most 是 great 的最高级，所以 mostly 的起点是「最大份额」，而不是笼统的「很多」。

normal.en: -ly comes from an Old English word for body or form, and it turns an adjective into a statement about manner.
normal.cn: -ly 出自古英语里表示身体或形貌的词，它把形容词变成说明「方式」的词。

normal.en: Almost is all plus most, a near total, and it sits beside mostly in the same family of degree words.
normal.cn: almost 是 all 加 most，表示接近全部，它与 mostly 并排站在同一族程度词里。

normal.en: Weather reports say mostly sunny because the forecast covers most of a region and most of a day, not every square metre or every minute.
normal.cn: 天气预报说 mostly sunny，因为预报覆盖的是一个地区的大部分和一天的大部分，而不是每一平方米、每一分钟。

normal.en: Mostly because names the leading reason among several, which is the same share logic applied to causes instead of things.
normal.cn: mostly because 指几个原因里最主要的那个，这正是把「份额」的逻辑从事物挪到了原因。

abstract.en: Picture a plate where rice fills most of the surface and two small side dishes take the corners.
abstract.cn: 想象一只盘子，米饭占去大半个盘面，两样小菜只占边角。

abstract.en: A word for the largest share keeps the minority visible: mostly means not entirely, so the rest is still there.
abstract.cn: 一个表示最大份额的词始终让少数派可见：mostly 意为「并非全部」，剩下的部分仍在。

abstract.en: Because it measures shares rather than absolutes, mostly fits sentences that report, estimate and predict, from weather to polls.
abstract.cn: 因为它衡量的是份额而不是绝对，mostly 特别适合报告、估计和预测的句子，从天气到民调都是。

examples.en: The trays on the counter were mostly empty by eight.
examples.cn: 到八点时，柜台上的托盘大半已经空了。

examples.en: She mostly works from home on Fridays.
examples.cn: 她周五通常在家工作。

examples.en: The report is mostly accurate, with two figures out of date.
examples.cn: 这份报告大体准确，只有两个数字过时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫斯特里」——大半时间都在忙，只剩一点才歇；记住 mostly 是大半、通常、几乎全部。

root: 古英语 māst（最多的，micel 的最高级）加副词词尾 -līce（后作 -ly）构成 mostli，中古英语起意为「大部分」；同族词有 most、almost、utmost、foremost，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the largest share; the senses divide into a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是最大份额；义项分出群体中的多数、习惯性的频率，以及数量上的接近全部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate where one dish covers most of the surface and small portions sit at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只盘子，一样菜占去大半，边上只留几小份。

branches.en: a tray with a few crumbs left on it
branches.cn: 只剩几点碎屑的托盘

branches.en: a hall where most seats are taken
branches.cn: 大半座位已坐了人的礼堂

branches.en: the early train taken on every working morning
branches.cn: 每个工作日早晨都坐的那班早车

branches.en: a bottle holding water with a thin layer of oil on top
branches.cn: 瓶里几乎全是水，只浮着一薄层油

branches.en: one adverb covering both how often a thing happens and how much of it there is
branches.cn: 同一个副词，既管事情多久发生一次，也管一样东西占了多少

intro.en: One Old English superlative, one adverbial ending and the English words built from them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语最高级、一个副词词尾，以及由它们构成的英语词，把这个词条撑了起来。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: mostly belongs to the Old English stock of degree words, and its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：mostly 属于古英语的程度词系统，其亲属词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 母亲；根源；像母亲般照顾
definition_en: a female parent, or the source of something
core_image: 母亲把洗好的校服晾在阳台，衣夹在风里轻轻碰响
scene: 母亲把洗好的校服晾在阳台，衣夹在风里轻轻碰响。My mother cooks on Sundays.
sceneCN: 这里 mother 是「母亲」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我妈妈周日做饭；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A female parent
senses.definition: A female parent
senses.definitionCN: 女性的父母
senses.example: My mother cooks on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 我妈妈周日做饭。
senses.why: Old English modor is a Germanic kinship word related to Latin mater; it names the female parent.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 modor 是日耳曼语亲属词，与拉丁语 mater 同源，指女性家长。

senses.title: The source or origin of something
senses.definition: The source or origin of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的来源
senses.example: Necessity is the mother of invention.
senses.exampleCN: 需要是发明之母。
senses.why: Because a mother gives life, the word was extended to anything that brings something else into being.
senses.whyCN: 因为母亲给予生命，这个词就扩展到任何使别的事物诞生的事物。

senses.title: To care for someone like a mother
senses.definition: To care for someone like a mother
senses.definitionCN: 像母亲一样照料
senses.example: She mothers the younger students.
senses.exampleCN: 她像母亲一样照顾低年级学生。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for the care a mother gives, often used of someone protective.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，指母亲般的照料，常指护着别人的人。

intro.en: The history of mother is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: mother 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

definition_en: a film shown in a cinema or on a screen, also the cinema as a place or an outing and the film industry as a whole

scene: 老街上的影院门口排起长队，售票窗口的灯还亮着。They queued outside the old cinema for a late-night movie.
sceneCN: 这里是「电影、影片」（第 1 个义项：放映的故事片）；句意为他们为一场深夜电影在旧影院外排队。图中可辨识物件：影院门口、排队的人群、售票窗。

senses.title: A film shown on a screen
senses.definition: a story or record told in moving images and sound, shown in a cinema or on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 用活动影像和声音讲述的故事或记录，在影院或屏幕上放映
senses.example: We watched a movie about a fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 我们看了一部关于渔村的电影。
senses.why: The word is a clipped form of moving picture, so the moving image itself is the starting point of every sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「活动的画面」的缩写，所以每一个义项都从「画面在动」这一点开始。

senses.title: The cinema as a place or an outing
senses.titleCN: 电影院；看电影这项活动
senses.definition: the cinema, or an occasion of going there to watch a film
senses.definitionCN: 电影院，或去那里看电影的一次活动
senses.example: They spent the afternoon at the movies.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一下午都泡在电影院里。
senses.why: Because a movie is what is shown, the plural the movies came to name the place and the outing built around it.
senses.whyCN: 因为被放映的东西是 movie，复数 the movies 就转而指放映它的场所，以及围绕它安排的一次出门。

senses.title: The film industry
senses.definition: the business of making and distributing films, especially in a particular country
senses.definitionCN: 制作与发行影片的行业，尤指某一国家的电影业
senses.example: He has worked in the movies for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在电影业干了三十年。
senses.why: A product made by many hands naturally names the whole trade that produces it, so the plural also stands for an industry.
senses.whyCN: 由许多人之手做出来的产品，自然会用来指生产它的整个行业，于是复数也代表一个产业。

senses.title: A short video made for any screen
senses.definition: a short filmed piece made for a phone, a website or a home screen rather than a cinema
senses.definitionCN: 为手机、网站或家庭屏幕而非影院制作的短小影片
senses.example: She made a short movie on her phone.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手机拍了一段短片。
senses.why: Once the word means moving images rather than a cinema release, any screen can host a movie, and length stops being essential.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指的是活动影像而不是影院上映，任何屏幕都能放映 movie，长度也就不再是必要条件。

intro.en: Movie is not an ancient word: it was cut down from moving picture in the early days of cinema and then spread from the screen to the place and the trade.
intro.cn: movie 并不是古词：它由早期的「活动的画面」缩短而来，随后从屏幕扩展到场所与行业。

items.en: The verb movere meant to move or set in motion, and it lies behind the English move inside moving picture.
items.cn: 动词 movere 意为移动、使动，它藏在 moving picture 里的英语 move 背后。

items.en: Old French movoir carried the Latin verb into English use and gave English the plain verb move.
items.cn: 古法语 movoir 把这个拉丁动词带入英语，给英语留下了朴素的动词 move。

items.en: The phrase moving picture was coined when photographs first appeared to move, and it described a new kind of show.
items.cn: 当照片第一次看上去会动时，人们造出 moving picture 这一说法，用来描述一种新的表演。

items.en: American speakers shortened moving picture to movie with the familiar -ie ending also seen in talkie, a film with sound.
items.cn: 美国使用者把 moving picture 缩短为 movie，用了熟悉的 -ie 词尾，带声音的影片 talkie 也用了这个词尾。

items.en: Modern English extends movie from the film itself to the cinema, the outing and the industry, and now to short videos on any screen.
items.cn: 现代英语把 movie 从影片本身扩展到电影院、看电影的出门活动与电影业，如今还指任何屏幕上的短片。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the move stem inside moving picture, while the near-meaning group collects other words for films and their showing.
note.cn: 形近组收「活动的画面」里那条表示移动的词干上的形式，近义组收其他指影片及放映的词。

entries.definition: To change position, the verb hidden inside moving picture.
entries.definitionCN: 改变位置；藏在 moving picture 里的动词。

entries.definition: An act of moving, or an organized group working for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的动作，或为某个目标组织起来的群体。

entries.definition: Changing position, or causing a strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 正在移动的，或引起强烈情感的。

entries.definition: A person who goes to the cinema, often regularly.
entries.definitionCN: 常去电影院看电影的人。

entries.definition: A motion picture, the word more common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 电影，英式用法中更常见的词。

entries.definition: A building where films are shown, or the art of making them.
entries.definitionCN: 放映影片的建筑，或制作影片的艺术。

entries.definition: A film, especially in older or informal British use.
entries.definitionCN: 影片，尤见于较早或非正式的英式用法。

entries.definition: Recorded film material, especially before it is edited.
entries.definitionCN: 拍摄下来的影像素材，尤指尚未剪辑的部分。

normalIntro.en: The word is a clipped compound, and its family keeps returning to the idea of images that move.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被截短的复合词，它的同族词也一直回到「画面会动」这个念头。

normal.en: Movie is moving picture cut short, with the -ie ending that also turned talking picture into talkie.
normal.cn: movie 是 moving picture 缩短而来，用的 -ie 词尾也曾把 talking picture 变成 talkie。

normal.en: The plural the movies names the place and the habit, not a pile of separate films.
normal.cn: 复数的 the movies 指场所与习惯，而不是一堆各自分开的影片。

normal.en: movie theater and movie star are compounds: one names the building, the other the person the screen makes famous.
normal.cn: movie theater 与 movie star 都是复合词：一个指建筑，一个指屏幕捧红的人。

normal.en: A moviegoer is simply movie plus goer, the person who goes.
normal.cn: moviegoer 就是 movie 加 goer，指去看电影的人。

normal.en: Latin movere, to move, sits far back inside the word, which is why the family is full of movement words.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 movere（移动）藏在这个词的很深处，所以这一族词里全是表示「动」的词。

abstract.en: Twenty-four pictures a second make a still photograph stand up and walk.
abstract.cn: 每秒二十四张画面，能让一张静止的照片站起来走路。

abstract.en: A dark hall, one beam of light, and a whole town living inside it for two hours.
abstract.cn: 一间暗厅，一束光，一整个小镇在里面过上两个小时。

abstract.en: The word began as a description of a trick and ended as the name of an industry.
abstract.cn: 这个词起初只是对一种戏法的描述，最后成了一个行业的名字。

examples.en: The movie was shot in a small mountain town.
examples.cn: 这部电影在一个山间小镇拍摄。

examples.en: We go to the movies most Fridays.
examples.cn: 我们大多数周五都去看电影。

examples.en: She wants to work in the movies after college.
examples.cn: 她想大学毕业后进入电影业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「木威」——一块木幕上放出很有威势的画面；记住 movie 是电影。

root: 一般认为 movie 是 moving picture（活动的画面）的缩写；moving 源自古法语 movoir、拉丁语 movere（移动），-ie 是英语指小词尾。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the film itself; the senses then divide into the place and the outing, the industry behind it, and the short video on any screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是影片本身；义项由此分出放映的场所与出门活动、背后的产业，以及任何屏幕上的短片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam of light cutting through a dark hall and landing on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光穿过黑暗的放映厅，落在幕布上。

branches.en: a beam of light crossing a dark hall
branches.cn: 一束光穿过黑暗的放映厅

branches.en: a queue forming outside a cinema
branches.cn: 影院外排起的队伍

branches.en: credits rolling over a crowded studio lot
branches.cn: 片尾字幕滚过拥挤的片场

branches.en: a short clip filmed on a phone
branches.cn: 用手机拍下的一段短片

branches.en: a late show that turns into a night out
branches.cn: 一场深夜电影变成一次夜游

intro.en: The word is a clipped compound resting on a Latin verb of motion, an English ending, and compounds that name the people and the buildings around films.
intro.cn: 这个词是被截短的复合词，依托一个表示运动的拉丁动词、一个英语词尾，以及为人和建筑命名的复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere and its noun motus name movement, and they are the distant source of the move inside moving picture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 movere 及其名词 motus 表示移动，是 moving picture 里 move 的遥远来源。
