definition_zh: 许多；大量；非常；…得多；差不多
definition_en: a large amount of something, to a great degree, and in fixed phrases nearly or hardly
core_image: 一只不断被添满的碗，米粒堆过了碗沿
scene: 工地上堆着还没搬完的砖，屋顶的瓦片只铺了一半。There is much work left before the roof is finished.
sceneCN: 这里是「许多、大量」（第 1 个义项：大量的事物）；句意为屋顶完工前还有大量活要干。图中可辨识物件：砖堆、半铺的屋顶、瓦片。

derivatives.zh: 由 much 加 -ness 构成，义为「大量；许多」，多见于固定说法 much of a muchness，意为彼此差不多
由 much 加 -ly 构成，非正式用语，义为「非常；大大地」
由前缀 over-（过度）加 much 构成，义为「过多的；过多地」

senses.title: A large amount of something
senses.definition: a large amount or quantity of something, especially with uncountable nouns
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的大量或许多，尤与不可数名词连用
senses.example: Much of the old town was rebuilt after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，老城的很大一部分被重建了。
senses.why: The Old English word meant great in size, and size easily becomes amount when the thing counted cannot be divided.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词本指体积大，而当所计的东西分不开时，体积就很容易变成数量。

senses.title: To a great degree
senses.definition: by a large amount, especially before comparatives or verbs of liking
senses.definitionCN: 大量地，尤用于比较级或表示喜好的动词之前
senses.example: I much prefer walking to driving in this weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这种天气里，我远更喜欢走路而不是开车。
senses.why: Once great size is abstracted, it can measure intensity rather than quantity, so the word starts to mean very or far.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「体积大」被抽象化，它就能衡量强度而非数量，于是这个词开始表示「很」或「远远」。

senses.title: Nearly, in fixed phrases
senses.definition: almost, used in phrases such as much the same or much as
senses.definitionCN: 几乎，用于 much the same 或 much as 一类短语
senses.example: The two maps are much the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这两张地图几乎一模一样。
senses.why: Two things that are much the same have come so close that the remaining difference is tiny, so greatness of degree turns into nearness.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西「大致相同」，说明它们靠得如此近，剩下的差别很小，于是程度之大转成了「接近」。

senses.title: Not a good example of a type, in negative phrases
senses.definition: used in not much of a to say that someone or something is a poor example of a type
senses.definitionCN: 用于 not much of a，表示某人或某物算不上某一类型的好例子
senses.example: He is not much of a cook, but he tries.
senses.exampleCN: 他算不上好厨师，但他肯尝试。
senses.why: If much measures amount, then not much of a thing measures a small amount of that quality, which is a polite way of saying it is poor.
senses.whyCN: 如果 much 衡量的是数量，那么 not much of a thing 就是衡量那种品质的数量很少，这是说它水准不高的委婉方式。

intro.en: Much descends from an Old English adjective for great, and its irregular more and most come from the same root rather than from -er and -est.
intro.cn: much 源自一个表示「大的」的古英语形容词，它的不规则比较级 more 与最高级 most 同出这一词根，而不是靠 -er 与 -est。

items.en: A reconstructed root generally written meg- meant great, and it also produced Latin magnus and Greek megas.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个常写作 meg- 的印欧语重构词根意为「大的」，它也产生了拉丁语 magnus 与希腊语 megas。

items.en: Old English mycel meant great or much, and its comparative and superlative were ma and mæst.
items.cn: 古英语 mycel 意为大的、多的，它的比较级与最高级是 ma 与 mæst。

items.en: Middle English shortened muchel to muche, and the clipped form much became standard.
items.cn: 中古英语把 muchel 缩短为 muche，截短后的 much 成为标准形式。

items.en: By the early modern period much was fixed for amount and degree, while more and most kept the old comparative and superlative.
items.cn: 到近代早期，much 已固定用来表示数量与程度，而 more 与 most 保留了古老的比较级与最高级。

items.en: Modern English much works as determiner, pronoun and adverb, and appears mainly in questions, negatives and fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语的 much 可作限定词、代词和副词，主要出现在疑问句、否定句和固定短语中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the irregular family built on the same old root, while the near-meaning group collects other quantity and degree words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一古老词根上的不规则词族，近义组收其他表示数量与程度的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of much, meaning a greater amount.
entries.definitionCN: much 的比较级，表示更大的量。

entries.definition: The superlative of much, meaning the greatest amount.
entries.definitionCN: much 的最高级，表示最大的量。

entries.definition: The quality of being much, used in much of a muchness.
entries.definitionCN: 「多」的性质，见于 much of a muchness。

entries.definition: More than is needed or wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 超过所需或所愿的。

entries.definition: A large number of countable things, the counterpart of much.
entries.definitionCN: 大量可数的事物，与 much 相对。

entries.definition: Enough or more than enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 足够或绰绰有余的量。

entries.definition: To a very large degree.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上；非常。

entries.definition: A large amount, in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中的大量。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old Germanic adjective of size that turned into a measure of amount and then of degree.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示体积的古老形容词，先变成数量的度量，再变成程度的度量。

normal.en: Old English mycel meant great, and its shortened descendant much kept the idea of a large mass.
normal.cn: 古英语 mycel 意为大的，缩短后的后代 much 保留了「一大团」的意思。

normal.en: More and most are not formed with -er and -est because they are relics of the old comparative and superlative.
normal.cn: more 与 most 不是用 -er 和 -est 构成的，因为它们是古老比较级与最高级的遗存。

normal.en: Much pairs with uncountable nouns such as water and time, while many pairs with things you can count.
normal.cn: much 与 water、time 这类不可数名词搭配，many 则与可以数的东西搭配。

normal.en: too much, very much and how much are fixed patterns that cover excess, intensity and quantity.
normal.cn: too much、very much 与 how much 是固定说法，分别覆盖过量、强度与数量。

normal.en: not much of a cook means a poor cook, because the phrase measures how little of the quality is present.
normal.cn: not much of a cook 意为算不上好厨师，因为这个说法衡量的是那种品质有多少。

abstract.en: A bowl that is filled past its rim is the picture behind every use of much.
abstract.cn: 一只堆过碗沿的碗，就是 much 每次使用背后的画面。

abstract.en: Size becomes amount, amount becomes intensity, and intensity becomes nearness: one root, three directions.
abstract.cn: 体积变成数量，数量变成强度，强度变成接近：一条根，三个方向。

abstract.en: English keeps the old irregular more and most as a reminder that this word is older than its grammar.
abstract.cn: 英语保留不规则的 more 与 most，提醒人这个词比它的语法规则更老。

examples.en: Much of the old town was rebuilt after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，老城的很大一部分被重建了。

examples.en: I much prefer walking to driving in this weather.
examples.cn: 这种天气里，我远更喜欢走路而不是开车。

examples.en: The two maps are much the same.
examples.cn: 这两张地图几乎一模一样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马吃」——马吃东西吃得多，就是许多；记住 much 是许多。

root: 古英语 mycel（大的、多的）经中古英语 muchel 缩短为 much；比较级 more、最高级 most 同出这一词根，一般认为与拉丁语 magnus 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a large amount; the senses then divide into a high degree, a nearness in fixed phrases, and the negative phrase that measures a poor example.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是大量；义项由此分出很高的程度、固定短语里的「接近」，以及衡量「算不上好」的否定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl filled again and again until the grain piles over its rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被反复添满的碗，米粒堆过了碗沿。

branches.en: a bowl filled past its rim
branches.cn: 一只堆过碗沿的碗

branches.en: a road chosen over a faster one
branches.cn: 放着更快的路不走，偏选这一条

branches.en: two maps laid side by side
branches.cn: 两张并排摊开的地图

branches.en: a kitchen trial that ends in smoke
branches.cn: 一次以浓烟收场的厨房尝试

branches.en: a store of grain that dwarfs the need
branches.cn: 一堆远超所需的粮食

intro.en: The word is an old adjective of size with an irregular comparative family, plus two English suffixes that build a noun and an adverb from it.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示体积的古老形容词，带着一个不规则比较级词族，另有两个英语后缀从它造出名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnus, magis and maximus belong to the same old root as much, even though English took the word through Germanic channels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magnus、magis 与 maximus 和 much 同出一个古老词根，尽管英语是经由日耳曼语渠道得到这个词的。

definition_zh: 谋杀；凶杀；谋杀罪；糟蹋；彻底击败
definition_en: the crime of killing a person deliberately; to kill someone unlawfully and on purpose; also, in loose use, to ruin a piece of work or defeat an opponent completely
core_image: 一只手的影子按在另一个人的影子上，把对方从地面上抹去
scene: 侦探在雨后的巷口拉起警戒线，墙角的脚印还湿着，围观的人低声说这不像意外。The detective read the report and concluded that the man had been murdered in his own kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里是「谋杀、蓄意杀害」（第 1 个义项：非法且故意地夺去他人性命）；句意为侦探看过报告后断定这名男子是在自家厨房里被杀害的。图中可辨识物件：警戒线、湿脚印、厨房门。

pos.zh: 蓄意杀害；糟蹋；彻底击败

derivatives.zh: 由 murder 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「凶手；谋杀者」
由 murder 加 -ous 构成，义为「蓄意杀人的；极其危险的」
由 murderer 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，义为「女凶手」

senses.title: The crime of killing a person on purpose
senses.definition: the crime of killing another person deliberately and unlawfully
senses.definitionCN: 非法且故意地杀害他人的罪行
senses.example: The trial lasted two weeks and ended in a verdict of murder.
senses.exampleCN: 审判持续了两周，最终裁定为谋杀。
senses.why: Old English morthor named a hidden killing, a death kept secret, so the word first recorded concealment rather than the weapon.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 morthor 指暗中进行的杀害，是「不让外人知道的死亡」，所以这个词最早记录的重点是隐秘，而不是凶器。

senses.title: To kill a person unlawfully and deliberately
senses.definition: to kill someone on purpose and against the law
senses.definitionCN: 故意且违法地夺去他人生命
senses.example: Police believe the same person murdered two shopkeepers.
senses.exampleCN: 警方认为同一个人杀害了两名店主。
senses.why: Once the noun named the hidden act, the verb could name doing it, and the law uses the pair to separate a planned killing from an accident.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然指这种隐秘的行为，动词就能指做出这种行为；法律用这一对词把有预谋的杀害与意外区分开。

senses.title: Murder as a charge in law
senses.definition: the offence itself as charged in court, carrying the heaviest penalty in many legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上被指控的罪名本身，在许多法律体系里对应最重的刑罚
senses.example: He was charged with murder and held without bail.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控谋杀，不得保释。
senses.why: Legal language turned the act into a countable charge, so murder can stand in a courtroom list beside theft and fraud.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言把这种行为变成一个可列举的罪名，于是 murder 能和盗窃、欺诈一起出现在法庭的罪名清单里。

senses.title: To ruin a performance or defeat an opponent badly
senses.definition: in informal use, to spoil a piece of work or beat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中把作品弄坏，或以很大差距击败对手
senses.example: The young pianist murdered the difficult passage but never lost the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻钢琴手把那一段难弹的乐句糟蹋了，却始终没有失去听众。
senses.why: The violent core image survives in slang as exaggeration: a singer who murders a song figuratively kills it, and the same hyperbole covers a heavy defeat.
senses.whyCN: 暴力的核心意象在俚语里以夸张的方式保留下来：歌手 murder 一首歌，就是把歌「弄死」了；同样的夸张也用来形容惨败。

intro.en: Murder is one of the oldest English words for killing, and its earliest use stresses secrecy rather than the manner of death.
intro.cn: murder 是英语里最古老的表示杀害的词之一，最早的用法强调的是隐秘，而不是死亡的方式。

items.en: Morthor named a secret killing, a death that the killer tried to hide, and the word kept that shadow of concealment.
items.cn: morthor 指私下进行的杀害，是凶手想要掩盖的死亡，这个词一直保留着隐瞒的阴影。

items.en: The verb morthrian meant to commit such a killing, and noun and verb travelled together into later English.
items.cn: 动词 morthrian 意为实施这类杀害，名词和动词一起进入了后来的英语。

items.en: Middle English murdren and murdre referred to both the act and the crime, and the modern spelling settled after the noun.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 murdren 与 murdre，兼指行为和罪名，现代拼写大致在名词之后固定下来。

items.en: Norman French gave English the legal pairing for a killing done with malice, and the courts kept murder apart from manslaughter.
items.cn: 诺曼法语给英语带来了「恶意杀害」的法律搭配，法庭把 murder 与过失杀人清楚分开。

items.en: Modern English keeps the criminal sense and adds a loose everyday sense in which a bad performance or a heavy defeat is called murder.
items.cn: 现代英语保留犯罪义，又加上日常的宽松用法，把糟糕的表演或惨败也称作 murder。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family of murder plus two words that merely share its shape; the near-meaning group collects other verbs and legal terms for killing.
note.cn: 形近组收 murder 的同族词，以及两个只是字形接近的词；近义组收其他表示杀害的动词与法律术语。

entries.definition: The person who commits a murder.
entries.definitionCN: 实施谋杀的人。

entries.definition: Capable of or intending to kill; extremely dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 有杀人意图的；极其危险的。

entries.definition: To speak quietly under the breath; only the shape resembles murder, the origins differ.
entries.definitionCN: 低声咕哝；只是字形接近 murder，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft, low sound; the spelling is close but the word has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 轻柔低沉的声音；拼写相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To cause someone or something to die.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物死亡。

entries.definition: To kill a prominent person, usually for political reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 通常出于政治原因刺杀要人。

entries.definition: To kill, especially violently, used mostly in old or literary texts.
entries.definitionCN: 杀害，尤指暴力杀害，多用于古旧或文学作品。

entries.definition: The killing of one person by another, whether lawful or not.
entries.definitionCN: 一人致另一人死亡，无论是否合法。

normalIntro.en: One old English noun of secret killing, its verb and its legal afterlife explain both the crime and the slang.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示暗中杀害的古英语名词、它的动词，以及它在法律里的延续，同时解释了罪名与俚语。

normal.en: Old English morthor meant a secret killing, so the word begins with concealment rather than with blood.
normal.cn: 古英语 morthor 意为暗中的杀害，所以这个词起点是「隐瞒」，而不是血。

normal.en: Murderer adds -er, the person, while murderous adds -ous, the quality; both stay inside the criminal family.
normal.cn: murderer 加 -er 指人，murderous 加 -ous 指性质，两者都留在犯罪这个词族里。

normal.en: The law keeps murder, deliberate, apart from manslaughter, without intent, and the pair still defines the charge.
normal.cn: 法律把表示故意的 murder 与表示无意的 manslaughter 分开，这一对词至今界定着罪名。

normal.en: Noun and verb share one idea, so you can commit a murder or murder a person with no change of meaning.
normal.cn: 名词与动词共用一个意思，所以 commit a murder 与 murder a person 含义不变。

normal.en: The slang sense survives because murder is extreme, and exaggeration borrows extreme words for bad singing and heavy defeat.
normal.cn: 俚语义能留下来，是因为 murder 足够极端；夸张正好借极端词来形容走调的演唱和惨败。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow pressing another shadow into the ground until it disappears.
abstract.cn: 想象一个影子把另一个影子按进地面，直到它消失。

abstract.en: A word for a hidden death reminds you that concealment, not noise, was the original danger.
abstract.cn: 一个表示暗中死亡的词提醒人：最早的危险是掩盖，而不是声响。

abstract.en: Because it names an irreversible act, murder can be borrowed only loosely for a spoiled song or a lost match.
abstract.cn: 因为它指的是一种不可逆的行为，所以只能宽松地借来说糟蹋一首歌或输掉一场比赛。

examples.en: The court found that she had murdered her business partner.
examples.cn: 法庭认定她谋杀了她的生意伙伴。

examples.en: He was charged with murder after the body was found.
examples.cn: 尸体被发现后，他被控谋杀。

examples.en: Our team murdered them in the second half.
examples.cn: 我们队在下半场把他们彻底击败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抹的」——把人从世上抹掉，就是 murder；记住它是谋杀。

root: 古英语 morthor（暗中的杀害）与动词 morthrian 构成，中古英语作 murdre，诺曼法语强化了法律用法；同族词有 murderer、murderous，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a killing kept secret; the senses divide into the crime, the act, the legal charge, and a slang exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是隐秘的杀害；义项分出罪行、行为、法律罪名，以及俚语里的夸张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shadow pressing another shadow flat against the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个影子把另一个影子按平在地面上。

branches.en: a strip of tape sealing off a dark doorway
branches.cn: 封住黑暗门洞的警戒带

branches.en: a story told to neighbours that nobody believes
branches.cn: 讲给邻居听却没人相信的说法

branches.en: a hand doing what the law forbids
branches.cn: 做了法律禁止之事的那只手

branches.en: a charge read aloud in a courtroom
branches.cn: 法庭上被宣读的一项罪名

branches.en: a song shouted off key into a microphone
branches.cn: 对着麦克风走调喊完的一首歌

intro.en: An Old English noun and verb of secret killing, two English suffixes and the modern compounds carry the entry.
intro.cn: 一个表示暗中杀害的古英语名词与动词、两个英语后缀，以及现代复合形式，撑起了这个词条。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: murder belongs to the Old English stock, and its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：murder 属于古英语词汇，其亲属词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 博物馆；陈列馆；馆藏机构；专门展室
definition_en: a building where objects of artistic, historical or scientific interest are collected, studied and shown to the public, and also the institution or collection itself
core_image: 玻璃柜里一排旧陶罐，被一盏小灯照出细密的裂纹
scene: 展厅里灯光压得很低，孩子们贴着玻璃柜找一只陶罐上的裂缝，讲解员说它在地下埋了很久。The city museum keeps a whole floor of pottery that was found beneath the old market.
sceneCN: 这里是「博物馆」（第 1 个义项：收藏并陈列文物或艺术品的场所）；句意为这座市立博物馆留出整整一层，陈列旧市场地下挖出的陶器。图中可辨识物件：玻璃柜、陶罐、射灯。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 mousa（缪斯）与 -logy（学说）构成，义为「博物馆学」
由 museology 加表示「人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「博物馆学专家」
与 museum 同源于缪斯，义为「沉思；冥想」

senses.title: A building that collects and displays objects
senses.definition: a building where objects of art, history or science are collected, kept and shown to the public
senses.definitionCN: 收藏、保存并向公众展示艺术、历史或科学物品的建筑
senses.example: The museum opens at nine and closes at five.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆九点开门，五点闭馆。
senses.why: Greek mouseion was a place of the Muses, a seat of learning, and the modern word still names a building that holds knowledge rather than sells goods.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mouseion 是缪斯女神的地方，也就是治学之所；现代这个词仍指收藏知识的建筑，而不是卖东西的场所。

senses.title: The institution or collection itself
senses.definition: the institution, or the collection it holds, considered apart from its building
senses.definitionCN: 把这个机构或它收藏的藏品单独来看，而不指建筑本身
senses.example: The museum lent three paintings to a show in another city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆把三幅画借给了另一座城市的展览。
senses.why: Because the collection travels while the building stays, the name moved from the place to the body that owns and cares for the objects.
senses.whyCN: 藏品可以出借巡展，而建筑留在原地，于是这个名称从「地方」转到「拥有并照管这些藏品」的机构。

senses.title: A room devoted to a special subject
senses.definition: a room or gallery set apart for a particular subject, often smaller than a full museum
senses.definitionCN: 为一个特定主题单独辟出的房间或展廊，通常比完整的博物馆小
senses.example: A small museum of typewriters sits above the bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 书店楼上有一间小小的打字机陈列室。
senses.why: When the gathering of objects was small and focused, English kept the same word for a single room, so a museum can be a cabinet-sized space for one subject.
senses.whyCN: 当收藏的对象又少又专时，英语仍用同一个词指单个展室，所以 museum 也可以是为一个主题办的小小空间。

intro.en: Museum goes back to the Greek mouseion, a place of the Muses, and it reached English through Latin and French as a name for a place of study.
intro.cn: museum 可追溯到希腊语 mouseion，即缪斯之地；它经拉丁语与法语进入英语，最初指治学之所。

items.en: Mousa, a Muse, named one of the goddesses of poetry, music and learning, and their shrines were places of the arts.
items.cn: mousa 即缪斯，是掌管诗歌、音乐与学问的女神，供奉她们的地方就是艺术之地。

items.en: Mouseion meant a place dedicated to the Muses, a seat of learning where books and objects were kept and discussed.
items.cn: mouseion 意为献给缪斯的地方，是保存并讨论书籍与器物的治学之所。

items.en: Latin borrowed mouseion as museum, keeping the sense of a study or a place of learned pursuits.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 mouseion 借作 museum，仍指书房或治学之所。

items.en: French musée carried the word into the language of galleries, where it named a place holding a collection open to visitors.
items.cn: 法语 musée 把这个词带进画廊的语言，指收藏并向参观者开放的地方。

items.en: Modern English fixes the idea of a public building, and the Greek word for Muse survives inside muse and music.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义固定为公共建筑，希腊语中「缪斯」这个词仍留在 muse 与 music 里面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Greek Muse and on the place ending -eum; the near-meaning group collects places and events that hold collections.
note.cn: 形近组收由希腊语「缪斯」与表地点的 -eum 词尾构成的词；近义组收收藏与展示藏品的场所和活动。

entries.definition: To think deeply about something, or a source of inspiration; the word shares the Greek Muse.
entries.definitionCN: 沉思，或灵感的来源；与希腊语缪斯同源。

entries.definition: Sounds arranged to be sung or played; the name comes through the Muses.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌唱或演奏而组织的声音；名称经由缪斯而来。

entries.definition: A picture made of small coloured pieces; the shape is close but the origin differs.
entries.definitionCN: 用小块彩色材料拼成的图画；字形相近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: A large, grand tomb; the ending looks alike but the word comes from a king's name.
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟的陵墓；词尾形似，但这个词来自一位国王的名字。

entries.definition: A room or building where art is shown.
entries.definitionCN: 陈列艺术品的房间或建筑。

entries.definition: A public display of objects or works.
entries.definitionCN: 公开展示物品或作品的活动。

entries.definition: A place or collection of records kept for study.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究保存档案的地方或收藏。

entries.definition: A group of objects gathered and kept together.
entries.definitionCN: 收集并放在一起的一组物品。

normalIntro.en: A Greek place of the Muses became a Latin study, a French gallery and an English public building; the entry follows that journey.
normalIntro.cn: 一个希腊的缪斯之地，先后变成拉丁语的书房、法语的画廊、英语的公共建筑；这个词条就沿着这条路展开。

normal.en: Mouseion was a place of the Muses, so a museum is first of all a home for knowledge, not a shop.
normal.cn: mouseion 是缪斯之地，所以 museum 首先是知识的住所，而不是店铺。

normal.en: The Muses cover poetry and music too, which is why muse and music sit in the same word family.
normal.cn: 缪斯也掌管诗歌与音乐，所以 muse 与 music 留在同一个词族里。

normal.en: -Eum is a place ending borrowed from Greek, so museum, mausoleum and gymnasium share a shape that marks a location.
normal.cn: -eum 是从希腊语借来的地点词尾，所以 museum、mausoleum、gymnasium 共有一个表示场所的形状。

normal.en: English keeps museum for the building, while a gallery can be a single room and a collection can travel.
normal.cn: 英语用 museum 指建筑，而 gallery 可以只是单个房间，collection 则可以出借巡展。

normal.en: Natural history museum joins the word with a subject, which shows the building can be named after what it holds.
normal.cn: natural history museum 把词与一个主题连起来，说明这类建筑可以用所藏之物来命名。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp over a glass case, one cracked pot lit from above.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照在玻璃柜上，一只裂了缝的陶罐被光从上方照亮。

abstract.en: A place named after goddesses of art suggests that objects are kept so they can be read, not merely stored.
abstract.cn: 一个以艺术女神命名的地方，说明藏品被保存下来是为了供人解读，而不只是堆放。

abstract.en: The word began with study and ended with visitors, so a museum is learning made public.
abstract.cn: 这个词从治学开始，以观众收尾，所以博物馆就是把学问向公众打开。

examples.en: The museum was closed for repairs all summer.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆整个夏天都在维修，暂停开放。

examples.en: We spent a rainy afternoon in the natural history museum.
examples.cn: 下雨的下午，我们待在自然史博物馆里。

examples.en: The museum lent its best painting to a foreign exhibition.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆把最好的一幅画借给了国外的展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缪泽姆」——缪斯女神住的地方，如今成了博物馆；记住 museum。

root: 希腊语 mousa（缪斯）→ mouseion（缪斯之地，治学之所）→ 拉丁语 museum → 法语 musée → 英语 museum；同族词有 muse、music、museology，没有另立的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place of the Muses; the senses divide into the public building, the institution and its collection, and a single room for one subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是缪斯之地；义项分出公共建筑、机构与馆藏，以及为单一主题设的展室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit glass case holding one cracked pot, with a guide and children in front of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：射灯照着玻璃柜里一只裂陶罐，柜前站着讲解员和孩子。

branches.en: a lit case holding one cracked pot
branches.cn: 射灯照着的一只裂陶罐

branches.en: a crate of paintings sent to another city
branches.cn: 一箱送往另一座城市参展的画

branches.en: a school class walking in behind a guide
branches.cn: 跟着讲解员走进展厅的一个班级

branches.en: a narrow room lined with old typewriters
branches.cn: 摆满旧打字机的狭长展室

branches.en: a name that covers both the walls and the treasures inside them
branches.cn: 一个既指墙壁、也指其中珍藏的名称

intro.en: A Greek noun for the Muses, a Greek place ending and the Latin and English forms built on them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个表示缪斯的希腊名词、一个希腊地点词尾，以及由它们构成的拉丁语与英语形式，撑起了这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin passed on the Greek place word as museum, so the Latin forms here are borrowings rather than native relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊的地点词转写为 museum，所以这里的拉丁形式是借词，而不是本土同族词。

items.meaning: art of sound through the Muses

latinEntries.meaning: a place of study, a library

definition_zh: 音乐；乐曲；乐声；配乐
definition_en: sound shaped by rhythm and melody into an art, together with the pieces it produces and the sound heard when it is performed
core_image: 一根琴弓划过琴弦，空气里浮出有秩序的声响
scene: 琴房里没开灯，雨点敲着窗，桌上一本摊开的乐谱被风翻动。The music from the old piano drifted down the empty corridor.
sceneCN: 这里是「音乐」（第 1 个义项：作为声音艺术的音乐）；句意为旧钢琴的乐声沿着空荡的走廊飘远。可辨识物件：钢琴、乐谱、雨中的窗。

derivatives.zh: 由 music 加 -al 构成，义为「音乐的；悦耳的」
由 music 加 -ian 构成，义为「音乐家；乐手」
由 musical 加 -ly 构成，义为「在音乐上；悦耳地」
由 musician 加 -ship 构成，义为「音乐修养；演奏水准」

senses.title: Organized sound treated as an art
senses.definition: sound arranged in rhythm and melody, made by voices or instruments and valued as an art
senses.definitionCN: 按节奏与旋律安排、由人声或乐器发出并被当作艺术的声音
senses.example: She studied music at the conservatory for four years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在音乐学院学了四年音乐。
senses.why: Greek mousike named the work of the Muses, so the word starts as a disciplined craft rather than as any noise that happens to be loud.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mousikē 原本指缪斯所掌管的技艺，所以这个词的起点是「有章法的技艺」，而不是碰巧很响的杂音。

senses.title: A piece or a body of written works
senses.definition: a particular composition, or the whole set of pieces written by one composer or within one style
senses.definitionCN: 某一首具体的作品，或某位作曲家、某种风格写下的全部作品
senses.example: The orchestra played music by Ravel and Debussy.
senses.exampleCN: 管弦乐队演奏了拉威尔与德彪西的作品。
senses.why: Because one noun can name both the art and the things made by that art, music also points to individual pieces you can put on a programme.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既能指这门艺术，也能指它做出的东西，因此 music 又可以指可以排进节目单的一首首具体作品。

senses.title: The sound actually heard in performance
senses.definition: the audible sound that reaches the ear when instruments or voices are playing
senses.definitionCN: 乐器或人声演奏时真正传到耳朵里的声音
senses.example: From the next room came the music of a violin.
senses.exampleCN: 隔壁房间传来小提琴的乐声。
senses.why: The abstract art becomes audible only at the moment of playing, so the same noun also names the physical sound filling the room.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的艺术只有在演奏的那一刻才变得可听，于是同一个名词也用来指充满房间的实际声响。

senses.title: Music laid under a film, game or ceremony
senses.definition: music used behind another activity to support its mood or mark its moments
senses.definitionCN: 垫在另一项活动之下、用来烘托气氛或标记节点的音乐
senses.example: The film's music does most of the emotional work.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的情绪多半由配乐承担。
senses.why: Once music is thought of as a layer under something else, the word takes the role of accompaniment, from cinema to a graduation ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 当音乐被看成垫在别的东西下面的一层，这个词就承担了伴奏的角色，从电影到毕业典礼都是如此。

intro.en: Music reaches English from the Greek art of the Muses by way of Latin and French, and its meaning widened from one craft to works, sound and accompaniment.
intro.cn: music 从希腊语中「缪斯的技艺」出发，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，词义也从一门技艺扩展到作品、声响与伴奏。

items.en: Mousike was the art presided over by the Muses and covered poetry, song and dance rather than instrumental playing alone.
items.cn: mousikē 是缪斯掌管的技艺，包括诗歌、歌唱与舞蹈，并不只指器乐演奏。

items.en: Latin took the word as musica and used it for the art of sound, one of the disciplines of the medieval schools.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词写作 musica，用来指声音的艺术，是中世纪学校里的学科之一。

items.en: Old French musique carried the word into everyday use for music and for the notation that records it.
items.cn: 古法语 musique 把这个词带入日常使用，既指音乐，也指记录音乐的谱子。

items.en: Middle English music named both the art and a written score, and the two meanings stayed side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语的 music 同时指这门艺术和一份写下的乐谱，两个含义并行了数百年。

items.en: Modern English adds the performed sound and the music written for films and ceremonies, so one word covers art, work, sound and setting.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上演奏出来的声响以及为电影、典礼写的配乐，一个词于是覆盖艺术、作品、声音与场景四层。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the forms built on this stem; the near-meaning group collects the things a piece of music is made of.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词干构成的同族形式；近义组收构成一段音乐的基本元素。

entries.definition: The adjective built on music with -al, meaning of music or sounding pleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 由 music 加 -al 构成的形容词，义为「音乐的」或「悦耳的」。

entries.definition: The person noun built on music with -ian, meaning one who plays or writes music.
entries.definitionCN: 由 music 加 -ian 构成的名词，指演奏或创作音乐的人。

entries.definition: The skill of a musician, formed by adding -ship to musician.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musician 后加 -ship 构成，指音乐家的演奏修养。

entries.definition: The adverb from musical, meaning in a way connected with music.
entries.definitionCN: 由 musical 派生出的副词，义为「在音乐方面」。

entries.definition: The sequence of notes that carries a tune.
entries.definitionCN: 承载曲调的连续音。

entries.definition: A short melody you can hum or whistle.
entries.definitionCN: 可以哼唱或吹出的短曲调。

entries.definition: A piece meant to be sung, words and music together.
entries.definitionCN: 为歌唱而作的作品，词与曲合一。

normalIntro.en: The word is the base of a small family, and the family shows how one noun grows an adjective, a person and a quality.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一小族词的基干，这一族词演示了一个名词如何长出形容词、人物名词和抽象品质。

normal.en: Music is the base of the family: add -al for the adjective musical, add -ian for the person musician.
normal.cn: music 是这一族词的基干：加 -al 得到形容词 musical，加 -ian 得到表示人的 musician。

normal.en: The Greek source mousike meant the art of the Muses, and museum comes from the same shrine, so the two words began as neighbours.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mousikē 意为缪斯的技艺，museum 也出自缪斯的神庙，两个词在源头上是邻居。

normal.en: Music is uncountable, so you say a piece of music or a lot of music, never a music.
normal.cn: music 不可数，所以要说 a piece of music 或 a lot of music，不能说 a music。

normal.en: Sheet music is the written notes rather than the sound, which is why the phrase turns up in every score shop.
normal.cn: sheet music 指纸上写下的音符而不是声响，所以这个说法总出现在卖乐谱的地方。

normal.en: Music to my ears is a fixed idiom for news that makes you glad to hear it.
normal.cn: music to my ears 是固定习语，指让人听了高兴的消息。

abstract.en: Picture the hush in a hall just before the conductor raises a hand: music is what fills that silence on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象音乐厅里指挥抬手前的那片安静：音乐就是有意填满这片安静的东西。

abstract.en: One noun covering art, works and background sound shows how deeply music is layered into ordinary days.
abstract.cn: 一个名词同时覆盖艺术、作品与背景声音，说明音乐早已层层嵌进平常的日子。

abstract.en: If you can hum it, it is already music, even before anyone writes it down.
abstract.cn: 只要你能把它哼出来，它就已经是音乐，哪怕还没有人把它记下来。

examples.en: She writes music for films and games.
examples.cn: 她为电影和游戏作曲。

examples.en: The music was so loud that we could feel the bass through the floor.
examples.cn: 音乐声太大，隔着地板都能感到低音的震动。

examples.en: He stood listening to the music of a street violinist.
examples.cn: 他站着听一位街头小提琴手的琴声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪齐克」：缪斯女神一抬手，音乐就响了；记住 music 是音乐。

root: 一般认为来自希腊语 mousikē（缪斯的技艺），经拉丁语 musica、古法语 musique 进入英语；同族词围绕「音乐」与「做音乐的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is organized sound valued as an art; from it the word reaches the works themselves, the sound heard while playing, and music placed under another activity.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被当作艺术的有序声音；由此分出具体的作品、演奏时听到的声响，以及垫在别的活动之下的配乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bow crossing a string and turning silence into ordered sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：琴弓划过琴弦，把寂静变成有秩序的声响。

branches.en: a practice room where scales slowly become a piece
branches.cn: 琴房里音阶慢慢连成一首曲子

branches.en: a shelf of scores filed under one composer's name
branches.cn: 按一位作曲家名字归档的一架乐谱

branches.en: an orchestra reading a new score for the first time
branches.cn: 乐团第一次读一份新总谱

branches.en: a violin's sound reaching the room next door
branches.cn: 小提琴的声音传到隔壁房间

branches.en: a soundtrack swelling under a closing scene
branches.cn: 片尾画面下渐渐涨起的配乐

intro.en: The family is built on the noun music plus two suffixes: -al for the adjective and -ian for the person, with Latin musica underneath all of them.
intro.cn: 这一族词建立在名词 music 之上，再加 -al 构成形容词、加 -ian 构成指人的名词，底下则是拉丁语 musica。

latinIntro.en: Latin musica came from Greek mousike and became the medieval European word for the art of sound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 musica 来自希腊语 mousikē，后来成为中世纪欧洲指「声音的艺术」的词。

items.meaning: a person who plays or writes music

latinEntries.meaning: of music, and also a musician

definition_zh: 音乐的；悦耳的；有音乐天赋的；音乐剧
definition_en: connected with music, pleasant to hear like music, gifted at music, and also a stage show built from songs and dialogue
core_image: 舞台幕布升起，歌声与对白在同一束灯光里交替
scene: 排练厅的灯亮到深夜，演员们把同一段合唱重复了一遍又一遍。The cast rehearsed the new musical until the lights went out.
sceneCN: 这里是「音乐剧」（第 3 个义项：歌曲与对白交替推进的舞台作品）；句意为演员们排练这部新音乐剧，直到灯都灭了。

pos.zh: 音乐的；悦耳的；有音乐天赋的

collocations.zh: 音乐剧剧场；音乐剧艺术

derivatives.zh: 由 musical 加 -ly 构成，义为「在音乐上；悦耳地」
由 musical 加 -ity 构成，义为「音乐性；音乐感」
由 music 加 -ian 构成，指「音乐家」，与 musical 同出 music，并非由 musical 派生

senses.title: Connected with music as an art
senses.definition: belonging to music, or used in the making and study of music
senses.definitionCN: 属于音乐的，或用于创作与研究音乐的
senses.example: She has a musical ear and can pick out a tune after one hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一双音乐的耳朵，听一遍就能把曲调挑出来。
senses.why: The Latin suffix -alis turned musica into musicalis, meaning 'belonging to music', so this sense is the plain label the suffix was made for.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -alis 把 musica 变成 musicalis，意思就是「属于音乐的」，所以这个义项正是该后缀的本职。

senses.title: Pleasant to hear, as if sung
senses.definition: sounding sweet and rhythmical, the way a well-made melody sounds
senses.definitionCN: 听起来甜美而有节奏，像一段做得好的旋律
senses.example: Their voices blended into a musical murmur.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的嗓音融成一片悦耳的低语。
senses.why: A sound orderly enough to resemble music earns the same adjective, so the word moves from 'belonging to music' to 'sounding like music' and becomes praise.
senses.whyCN: 一种声音只要有序到近似音乐，就能用同一个形容词，于是词义从「属于音乐」滑到「像音乐一样好听」，变成一句称赞。

senses.title: A stage or screen work of songs and dialogue
senses.definition: a play or film in which songs and spoken scenes alternate, usually with dancing
senses.definitionCN: 歌曲与说白交替出现、通常还带舞蹈的舞台剧或影片
senses.example: The cast rehearsed the new musical until the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们排练这部新音乐剧，直到灯都灭了。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century playbills shortened musical comedy to musical, and the adjective became a noun for an entire kind of show.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的戏单把 musical comedy 缩成 musical，这个形容词于是名词化，指一整类舞台作品。

senses.title: Gifted at music or sensitive to it
senses.definition: naturally aware of pitch and rhythm, or able to play and sing well
senses.definitionCN: 天生对音高与节奏敏感，或演奏演唱得好
senses.example: Even as a child he was unusually musical.
senses.exampleCN: 他小时候就显露出不寻常的音乐天赋。
senses.why: A person whose ear is tuned to music is described by the same adjective, so the word shifts from the art itself to the gift in the person.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵对音乐敏感的人也用这个形容词来描述，于是词义从艺术本身转到人身上的天赋。

intro.en: Musical is the adjective built on Latin musica with the suffix -alis; its noun use for a stage show came much later, from the theatre.
intro.cn: musical 是用后缀 -alis 加在拉丁语 musica 上构成的形容词；指舞台作品的名词用法要晚得多，来自剧院。

items.en: The Greek adjective mousikos described anything of the Muses, including a person trained in song and dance.
items.cn: 希腊语形容词 mousikos 形容一切属于缪斯的东西，也包括受过歌唱与舞蹈训练的人。

items.en: Latin kept musica for the art itself, the noun from which a whole set of adjectives could be built.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 musica 指这门艺术本身，这个名词后来又长出一整组形容词。

items.en: Musicalis added -alis to musica and meant simply 'relating to music', with no hint yet of the stage.
items.cn: musicalis 在 musica 后加 -alis，意思只是「与音乐有关的」，当时还没有舞台的含义。

items.en: Middle French passed musical to English, where it first described anything of music, from voices to instruments.
items.cn: 中古法语把 musical 传给英语，英语最初用它形容一切与音乐有关的东西，从嗓音到乐器。

items.en: In the nineteenth century musical was clipped from musical comedy and became a noun for a show of songs and spoken scenes.
items.cn: 十九世纪，musical 由 musical comedy 缩略而来，变成指「歌曲与说白并存的舞台作品」的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjective's own family and adverbs; the near-meaning group collects words for sounds that please the ear.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词的同族形式与副词；近义组收形容声音悦耳的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective is built on, naming the art of sound.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所依附的名词，指声音的艺术。

entries.definition: The person noun from the same base, formed with -ian rather than -al.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的指人名词，用 -ian 而非 -al 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb built on musical with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musical 后加 -ly 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The noun built on musical with -ity, naming the quality of being musical.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musical 后加 -ity 构成的名词，指音乐性。

entries.definition: Relating to melody, or pleasant because of its melody.
entries.definitionCN: 与旋律有关的；因旋律而动听的。

entries.definition: Having a pleasant tune that is easy to hear and follow.
entries.definitionCN: 曲调优美、容易听清的。

entries.definition: Sweet-sounding, like a well-sung melody.
entries.definitionCN: 音调甜美的，像唱得好的旋律。

normalIntro.en: The adjective sits between the noun music and the person musician, and its suffixes show which one you mean.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词夹在名词 music 与指人的 musician 之间，后缀决定你指的是哪一边。

normal.en: The suffix -al turns the noun music into the adjective musical, just as nation becomes national.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 把名词 music 变成形容词 musical，就像 nation 变成 national 一样。

normal.en: The -al ending marks a quality, while -ian marks a person, which is the clean line between musical and musician.
normal.cn: -al 结尾标记性质，-ian 结尾标记人物，这就是 musical 与 musician 之间清楚的分界。

normal.en: The noun musical began as a short form of musical comedy on nineteenth-century playbills.
normal.cn: 名词 musical 起初是十九世纪戏单上 musical comedy 的缩略形式。

normal.en: A musical instrument is any instrument used for music, a fixed phrase that pins the adjective to its first sense.
normal.cn: a musical instrument 指任何用于音乐的乐器，这个固定搭配把形容词钉在第一个义项上。

normal.en: Musicality is musical plus -ity: the quality of having a musical ear, named as a noun.
normal.cn: musicality 是 musical 加 -ity，把「有音乐耳朵」这种性质变成名词。

abstract.en: One adjective describing a sound, a show and a person's ear shows how a single idea spreads over three very different things.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既能形容声音、又能形容演出、还能形容人的耳朵，说明一个想法可以铺开到三种很不同的事物上。

abstract.en: When applause follows a song, the adjective quietly turns into a noun without changing a single letter.
abstract.cn: 歌声之后掌声响起，这个形容词便悄悄变成名词，一个字母都没改。

abstract.en: Calling a voice musical is a compliment that measures a human sound against an art form.
abstract.cn: 说一副嗓音 musical，是拿人的声音去比照一门艺术，本身就是称赞。

examples.en: The musical instruments were stored in a padded case.
examples.cn: 乐器被存放在一个带衬垫的箱子里。

examples.en: Her speaking voice is low and musical.
examples.cn: 她说话的声音低沉而悦耳。

examples.en: Tickets for the new musical sold out within a week.
examples.cn: 这部新音乐剧的门票一周内售罄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪齐扣」：缪斯一开口，歌声就扣住人；记住 musical 是音乐的、音乐剧。

root: 一般认为来自晚期拉丁语 musicalis（由 musica 加 -alis 构成），经中古法语 musical 进入英语；名词「音乐剧」是 musical comedy 的缩略。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts as a plain label for anything of music; it then stretches to sounds that please the ear, to a person's ear for music, and finally becomes a noun for a stage show.
sensesIntro.cn: 形容词最初只是「与音乐有关」的标签；随后扩展到悦耳的声音、人的音乐耳朵，最后名词化为一种舞台作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage curtain rising on a song that carries the story forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台幕布升起，一首歌把故事往前推。

branches.en: a rehearsal room with a piano and a metronome
branches.cn: 摆着钢琴与节拍器的排练房

branches.en: a voice so smooth that the room goes quiet
branches.cn: 嗓音顺滑到让整个房间安静下来

branches.en: a child picking out a tune by ear
branches.cn: 孩子凭耳朵挑出一段曲调

branches.en: a curtain rising on dancers and singers
branches.cn: 幕布升起，舞者与歌者同台

branches.en: an audition settled by the quality of a voice
branches.cn: 由嗓音好坏决定结果的试演

intro.en: The adjective is music plus -al, and two further suffixes, -ly and -ity, turn it into an adverb and a quality noun.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是 music 加 -al，再加 -ly 与 -ity 两个后缀，就得到副词和表示性质的名词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin musicalis is the direct model: musica plus -alis, meaning simply belonging to music.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 musicalis 是直接的样板：musica 加 -alis，意思就是「属于音乐的」。

latinEntries.meaning: of music, and also a musician

definition_zh: 音乐家；乐手；演奏者；有音乐才华的人
definition_en: a person who plays, writes or performs music, whether as a profession or as a gift
core_image: 一个人坐在琴凳上，手指在琴键上找到下一个音
scene: 地铁通道人来人往，一个抱着吉他的年轻人靠墙站着，脚边是敞开的琴盒。The musician played for the commuters and never once looked up.
sceneCN: 这里是「乐手、演奏者」（第 2 个义项：在乐队或公共场合演奏的人）；句意为那位乐手为来往的通勤者演奏，始终没有抬头。

derivatives.zh: 由 musician 加 -ship 构成，义为「音乐修养；演奏水准」
由 music 加 -al 构成，与 musician 同出 music，并非由 musician 加后缀而来
musician 由 music 加表示「从事某事的人」的 -ian 构成，因此 music 是它的基干，义为「音乐」

senses.title: Someone who makes music as a profession
senses.definition: a person who plays an instrument or writes music as a job, usually trained and paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 以演奏乐器或创作音乐为职业、通常受过训练并因此获得报酬的人
senses.example: He spent thirty years as a musician in the city orchestra.
senses.exampleCN: 他在市立管弦乐团当了三十年音乐家。
senses.why: The suffix -ian marks a person who practises an art, as in historian and librarian, so musician is simply the person slot of the music family.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ian 标记从事某门技艺的人，historian、librarian 都是如此，所以 musician 就是「音乐」这一族词里指人的那个位置。

senses.title: A player within a band or orchestra
senses.definition: one of the players in a group, named by the part or instrument they take rather than by fame
senses.definitionCN: 乐队或乐团里的成员，按其声部或乐器来称呼，而不论名气
senses.example: The band's musicians tuned up before the doors opened.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队的乐手们在开门前调好了音。
senses.why: A group needs named roles, so the same word narrows to the players on stage, each holding one instrument and covering one part.
senses.whyCN: 一个团体需要有名有姓的分工，于是同一个词收窄为台上的演奏者，每人持一件乐器、负责一个声部。

senses.title: Someone with a gift for music, paid or not
senses.definition: a person unusually good at music, whether or not it is their job
senses.definitionCN: 在音乐上格外出色的人，不论是否以此为业
senses.example: My grandmother was a fine musician and played at every family wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 我祖母是一位出色的音乐人，家里每场婚礼她都演奏。
senses.why: Because the word names ability as well as employment, it can praise an amateur whose playing is good enough to deserve the title.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指职业也指能力，所以也能用来称赞一位演奏水平够得上这个称号的业余爱好者。

intro.en: Musician names the person of the music family; English built it with -ian on the model of the Old French person noun.
intro.cn: musician 是「音乐」这一族词里指人的那个；英语仿照古法语的指人名词，用 -ian 把它构成。

items.en: The Greek noun mousike named the art of the Muses, and a person devoted to that art was already called mousikos.
items.cn: 希腊语名词 mousikē 指缪斯的技艺，献身于这门技艺的人当时就被称作 mousikos。

items.en: Latin kept musica for the art, while musicus could serve both as an adjective and as a name for a musician.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 musica 指这门艺术，而 musicus 既能作形容词，也能直接指乐师。

items.en: Old French musique named the art and became the base for a separate word for the person who practises it.
items.cn: 古法语 musique 指这门艺术，并成为另一个指「从事此艺者」的词的基础。

items.en: Musicien added -ien to musique and named the player or writer of music, the form English met in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: musicien 在 musique 后加 -ien，指演奏或创作音乐的人，英语在十四世纪接触到这个词形。

items.en: English kept the stem and put its own -ian in place of -ien, giving musician, the spelling and ending used ever since.
items.cn: 英语保留词干，把本族惯用的 -ian 换进 -ien 的位置，得到 musician，这个拼写与词尾沿用至今。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the nouns and adverbs of the same family; the near-meaning group collects the roles inside the music trade.
note.cn: 形近组收同一族里的名词与副词；近义组收音乐行业内部的不同角色。

entries.definition: The base noun of the family, naming the art itself.
entries.definitionCN: 这一族词的基干名词，指艺术本身。

entries.definition: The adjective from the same base, built with -al instead of -ian.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词，用 -al 而非 -ian 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a musical way, built on musical with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以音乐的方式」的副词，由 musical 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Musician plus -ship, naming the skill rather than the person.
entries.definitionCN: musician 加 -ship，指技艺而不是人。

entries.definition: Someone who plays or sings in front of an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前演奏或演唱的人。

entries.definition: A person who writes music rather than only playing it.
entries.definitionCN: 写音乐而不只是演奏的人。

entries.definition: A musician who plays an instrument rather than sings.
entries.definitionCN: 演奏乐器而非演唱的音乐人。

normalIntro.en: The word is the person slot of the music family, and the suffixes around it show skill, art and base.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「音乐」这一族词里指人的位置，周围的后缀分别标出技艺、艺术与基干。

normal.en: Musician is music plus -ian, the same suffix that makes historian and librarian into people.
normal.cn: musician 是 music 加 -ian，同一个后缀也把 historian、librarian 变成指人的词。

normal.en: The Old French original was musicien; English kept the stem and swapped the ending for its own -ian.
normal.cn: 古法语原形是 musicien，英语保留词干，把词尾换成本族惯用的 -ian。

normal.en: Musicianship is musician plus -ship, naming the skill rather than the person who has it.
normal.cn: musicianship 是 musician 加 -ship，指技艺而不是拥有技艺的人。

normal.en: A street musician is a fixed phrase for someone who plays in public for coins and attention.
normal.cn: street musician 是固定说法，指在公共场所演奏、靠路人投币与围观为生的人。

normal.en: A session musician is hired for a single recording or tour, which shows the word covers many kinds of paid work.
normal.cn: session musician 指只为一次录音或巡演受雇的乐师，说明这个词覆盖多种有偿工作。

abstract.en: Behind every musician stands a long room of scales that nobody ever clapped for.
abstract.cn: 每位音乐家背后都有一间长长的琴房，里面是无人喝彩的音阶。

abstract.en: The word moves easily between a star on a poster and a neighbour with a guitar, because ability is the real test.
abstract.cn: 这个词能轻易地从海报上的明星滑到隔壁抱吉他的邻居，因为真正的标准是能力。

abstract.en: If music is the art, the musician is the pair of hands that makes the art audible.
abstract.cn: 如果说音乐是那门艺术，音乐家就是让艺术变得可听的那双手。

examples.en: He spent thirty years as a musician in the city orchestra.
examples.cn: 他在市立管弦乐团当了三十年音乐家。

examples.en: The band's musicians tuned up before the doors opened.
examples.cn: 乐队的乐手们在开门前调好了音。

examples.en: My grandmother was a fine musician and played at every family wedding.
examples.cn: 我祖母是一位出色的音乐人，家里每场婚礼她都演奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪吉申」：缪斯女神一附身，人就成了乐手；记住 musician 是音乐家。

root: musician 由 music 加 -ian 构成，-ian 表示「从事某事的人」；这一构词仿照古法语 musicien，而 music 一般认为来自希腊语 mousikē（缪斯的技艺），经拉丁语 musica 传入。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person whose life is music; the senses split into the trained professional, the player in a group, and anyone whose gift earns the name.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「以音乐为业的人」；义项分成受过训练的职业音乐家、团体里的乐手，以及凭才华配得上这个称呼的任何人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a player at the keyboard, fingers finding the next note by ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：演奏者坐在琴前，手指凭耳朵找到下一个音。

branches.en: a cellist signing a season contract with an orchestra
branches.cn: 大提琴手与乐团签下一季合同

branches.en: a guitarist tuning backstage while the band waits
branches.cn: 吉他手在后台调音，乐队等着他

branches.cn: 祖母在婚礼上分文不取地演奏

branches.en: a street player whose ear is as sharp as any graduate's
branches.cn: 街头乐手的耳朵不输任何科班出身的人

intro.en: The person noun is music plus -ian, the same suffix that builds historian and librarian; -ship then turns the person into a quality.
intro.cn: 这个指人的名词由 music 加 -ian 构成，同一个后缀也造出 historian、librarian；再加 -ship 则把人变成一种修养。

latinIntro.en: Latin musica is the source of the whole family, and Latin musicus could already name a musician as well as describe music.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 musica 是整族词的源头，而拉丁语 musicus 既能形容音乐，也已经可以指乐师。

items.meaning: a person who plays or writes music

latinEntries.meaning: of music, and also a musician

definition_zh: 必须；一定；必需品
definition_en: used to say that something is necessary or almost certainly true; as a noun, something that cannot be left out
core_image: 一道关着的闸门，旁边只留一条必须走过去的通道
scene: 地铁入口处，安检员抬手示意乘客停下，把背包放上检查带。You must put your bag on the belt before you walk through.
sceneCN: 这里是「必须、有义务」（第 1 个义项：被要求做某事）；句意为过闸之前你得出示并放下背包接受检查。图中可辨识物件：闸门、检查带、背包。

collocations.zh: 一定做过（对过去的推测）

derivatives.zh: 由 must 与 have 复合，义为「必备品」
由 must 与 see 复合，义为「必看之物」

senses.title: To be obliged to do something
senses.definition: used to say that a person is obliged or forced to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人有义务或不得不做某事
senses.example: You must show your ticket at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须在门口出示车票。
senses.why: Old English moste was the past of motan and often meant had to; the old sense of permission narrowed into a demand, so the word now states an obligation rather than an option.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 moste 是 motan 的过去式，常表示「当时不得不」；原先的许可义收窄成强制义，所以这个词现在陈述的是义务，而不是选项。

senses.title: To be very likely true
senses.definition: used to say that something is almost certainly true, judging from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 依据证据判断某事几乎肯定成立
senses.example: The lights are off; they must have gone home.
senses.exampleCN: 灯都灭了，他们一定已经回家了。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be avoided, the mind treats the conclusion as unavoidable too, so the force of obligation slides into inference about what has to be the case.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事无法回避，人心也会把相应结论看成躲不开的，于是义务的力量滑向「情况必然如此」的推断。

senses.title: Something that cannot be left out
senses.definition: a thing that is absolutely necessary or strongly recommended
senses.definitionCN: 绝对必要或强烈建议不可省略的事物
senses.example: A torch is a must when you camp in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 在山里露营，手电是必备的。
senses.why: The noun keeps the force of the modal: anything called a must is treated as something one cannot skip, which is how a demand turns into an object on a packing list.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法保留了情态动词的力量：被称作 a must 的东西，被当成不能跳过的事物，于是一项要求就变成了清单上的一个物件。

intro.en: Must grew out of an Old English verb for being able or allowed; its past tense took over the present meaning of obligation.
intro.cn: must 源自古英语中表示「能够、被允许」的动词，它的过去式后来接管了现在时的义务义。

items.en: The verb reconstructed as motan is generally thought to have meant to have room or power to do something.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 motan 意为「有做某事的余地或力量」。

items.en: Motan meant to be able or to be permitted, and its past tense moste often carried the practical sense of having to.
items.cn: motan 意为能够或被允许，其过去式 moste 常带有「只好、不得不」的实感。

items.en: Moste spread into more contexts than the old present form, and speakers began to use it for present obligations.
items.cn: moste 的使用范围超过了旧的现在式，说话人开始用它表达当下的义务。

items.en: Must settled as an unchanging present form, took a contracted negative mustn't, and lost the old infinitive and participle.
items.cn: must 固定为没有词形变化的现在式，出现缩略否定 mustn't，旧的动词不定式和分词形式逐渐消失。

items.en: Modern English adds the inference use and the countable noun a must, plus compounds such as must-have and must-see.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了推测用法和可数名词 a must，还产生 must-have、must-see 这类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the negative contraction and three words that only resemble must in spelling; the near-meaning group holds other ways of expressing obligation.
note.cn: 形近组收 must 的否定缩略式，以及三个只是拼写相似、来源不同的词；近义组收其他表示义务的说法。

entries.definition: The contracted negative of must, common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: must 的否定缩略形式，口语中常见。

entries.definition: To gather people or courage for a purpose; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 召集人员或鼓起勇气；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A yellow sharp condiment made from seeds; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 用种子制成的黄色辛辣调味酱；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Smelling damp and stale, as an old room does; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 有潮湿霉味的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Expresses external obligation like must, but uses do in questions and negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 与 must 一样表示外在义务，但疑问和否定要借助 do。

entries.definition: Gives advice or a mild duty rather than a firm demand.
entries.definitionCN: 给出建议或轻微责任，语气不如 must 强硬。

entries.definition: States a duty seen as right, often in careful or written English.
entries.definitionCN: 表示按道理应尽的责任，多见于正式或书面英语。

entries.definition: Names a requirement, usually followed by to before a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指出一项需求，动词前通常带 to。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic modal that drifted from permission to obligation, with a negative contraction and two modern compounds around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语情态动词，从许可漂移到义务，周围还有一个否定缩略式和两个现代复合词。

normal.en: Old English motan meant to be able or allowed, and its past moste meant had to; must is that past form grown into a present.
normal.cn: 古英语 motan 意为能够、被允许，其过去式 moste 意为不得不；must 就是这个过去式长成了现在式。

normal.en: Must is followed by the bare verb: must go, never must to go.
normal.cn: must 后面直接跟动词原形：说 must go，不说 must to go。

normal.en: Mustn't forbids, while can't denies a guess: you mustn't smoke here, but he can't be at home.
normal.cn: mustn't 表示禁止，can't 才用来否定推测：此处不许吸烟，而「他不可能在家」要用 can't。

normal.en: Must have done looks back at a past certainty, which is why the perfect follows must, not the past tense.
normal.cn: must have done 回看一件过去确定的事，所以 must 后面接完成式，而不是过去式。

normal.en: The noun a must copies the modal's force: a must-have item is one you cannot leave out.
normal.cn: 名词 a must 沿用了情态动词的力量：a must-have item 就是不能省略的东西。

abstract.en: A gate that only opens one way turns an old permission word into a word of compulsion.
abstract.cn: 一道只能单向打开的闸门，把旧的许可词变成了强制词。

abstract.en: When no other route exists, a demand and a certainty feel like the same pressure.
abstract.cn: 当没有别的路可走，一项要求和一种确定感会显得是同一种压力。

abstract.en: Every packing list is a small museum of things someone decided they could not do without.
abstract.cn: 每一张行李清单，都是「有人认定不能没有」的小小陈列馆。

examples.en: Visitors must sign in at the front desk.
examples.cn: 访客必须在前台登记。

examples.en: She must have missed the last bus.
examples.cn: 她一定是错过了末班车。

examples.en: A good pair of gloves is a must in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天一副好手套是必备的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马斯特」——教练马斯特站在跑道边说：必须跑完这一圈；must 就是必须。

root: 古英语 motan（能够、被允许），过去式 moste 逐渐固定为 must；一般认为与德语 müssen 同出原始日耳曼语 motan，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unavoidable demand; from it grow the inference about what must be true and the noun for a thing one cannot leave out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是躲不开的要求；由此长出「情况必然如此」的推断，以及指「不能省略之物」的名词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate with only one open passage, where stopping is not an option.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道只留一条通道的闸门，停下不在选项之内。

branches.en: a guard raising a hand at the entrance
branches.cn: 入口处抬手示意的安检员

branches.en: a bag opened before the belt
branches.cn: 放上检查带之前的背包

branches.en: a dark window and a guess about who is inside
branches.cn: 暗着的窗和关于里面是谁的猜测

branches.en: a note that reads had to, written as must
branches.cn: 把「不得不」写成 must 的便条

branches.en: a torch placed first in the camp bag
branches.cn: 露营包里最先放手电的位置

intro.en: The word rests on one Old English modal, its past form, a negative clitic, and two modern compounds that turn the modal into a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的一个情态动词、它的过去式、一个否定附着成分，以及两个把情态动词变成名词的现代复合词支撑。

latinIntro.en: Must belongs to the Germanic modals, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: must 属于日耳曼语情态动词，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to be able, to be permitted
was able, was allowed, had to

definition_zh: 我的；用于感叹或称呼
definition_en: belonging to the speaker; also used in exclamations and in polite forms of address
core_image: 一只手把一件东西按在自己胸前，表示这件东西归我
scene: 门口的木架上挂着两件外套，一件深蓝，一件灰色。My coat is the blue one hanging by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「我的」（第 1 个义项：表示所属）；句意为挂在门边的那件蓝色外套是我的。图中可辨识物件：木架、两件外套、门。

pos.zh: 我的（形容词性物主代词）

derivatives.zh: my 的名词性形式，后面不接名词，义为「我的（东西）」
my 与 self 结合而成的反身代词，义为「我自己」

senses.title: Belonging to the speaker
senses.definition: belonging to the person who is speaking, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 属于说话人，用在名词之前
senses.example: My coat is the blue one hanging by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 挂在门边的那件蓝色外套是我的。
senses.why: Old English min was the genitive of the first person; a shortened form took over before nouns, so the word now points at an owner rather than naming a person.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 min 是第一人称的属格形式；一个缩短的形式在名词前占了上风，于是这个词现在指向所有者，而不是称呼某个人。

senses.title: Used in exclamations
senses.definition: used at the start of an exclamation to show surprise or dismay
senses.definitionCN: 放在感叹句开头，表示惊讶或不安
senses.example: My goodness, that was a close call.
senses.exampleCN: 天哪，刚才真是好险。
senses.why: The owner word became a way to put the speaker at the centre of a reaction, so my goodness means the surprise belongs to me, not to the thing seen.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示所有者的词变成了把说话人放在反应中心的手段，所以 my goodness 意味着惊讶属于我，而不是属于看到的东西。

senses.title: Used in polite address
senses.titleCN: 用于称呼（如亲爱的、大人）
senses.definition: used before a title or a term of address in courteous or old-fashioned speech
senses.definitionCN: 用于礼貌或老派的称呼之前
senses.example: My dear friend, you have nothing to worry about.
senses.exampleCN: 亲爱的朋友，你没有什么可担心的。
senses.why: A speaker who calls someone my dear marks that person as belonging to his circle of care, which is why the owner word turned into a marker of warmth.
senses.whyCN: 说话人叫对方 my dear，是把对方划进自己关心的圈子，这个表所属的词因此变成了表示亲切的标记。

intro.en: My is the genitive of the English first person, shortened from an Old English form that also produced mine.
intro.cn: my 是英语第一人称的属格形式，由古英语的一个形式缩短而来，mine 也出自同一来源。

items.en: A first person stem reconstructed with the shape me- is generally taken as the source of the possessive forms across the family.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构为 me- 的第一人称词干是整个语族中各种所有格形式的来源。

items.en: The possessive was reconstructed as minaz, marked for the speaker and agreeing with the thing owned.
items.cn: 所有格被重构为 minaz，既标记说话人，也随被拥有之物变化。

items.en: Old English used min before nouns and as a standalone form, with different endings for gender and number.
items.cn: 古英语用 min 放在名词前，也可单独使用，并随性与数变化词尾。

items.en: Middle English shortened min to mi before consonants and kept mine before vowels, a pattern still visible in the modern pair.
items.cn: 中古英语在辅音前把 min 缩成 mi，在元音前保留 mine，这一分别仍留在现代的一对形式里。

items.en: Modern English fixed my before nouns and mine on its own, and the two stopped differing by the following sound.
items.cn: 现代英语固定为名词前用 my、单独用 mine，两者不再随后面音素区分。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the nominal possessive and the reflexive built on the same stem, plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group collects other possessives.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的名词性所有格与反身代词，另加一个只是外形相似的词；近义组收其他所有格形式。

entries.definition: The possessive used without a following noun.
entries.definitionCN: 后面不接名词的名词性所有格，义为「我的」。

entries.definition: The object form of the first person singular.
entries.definitionCN: 第一人称单数的宾格形式。

entries.definition: The reflexive pronoun built from the same possessive stem.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一所有格词干构成的反身代词。

entries.definition: Short sight, from a Greek word for squinting; only the opening looks alike.
entries.definitionCN: 近视，源自希腊语「眯眼」；只是开头拼写相似，词源不同。

entries.definition: Belonging to the speaker together with others.
entries.definitionCN: 属于说话人以及其他人；我们的。

entries.definition: Belonging to the person spoken to.
entries.definitionCN: 属于听话的人；你的。

entries.definition: Belonging to people or things already mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已提到的人或物；他们的。

entries.definition: Belonging to a male person already mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已提到的男性；他的。

normalIntro.en: The word is the short form of an Old English possessive, and its longer relative survives as mine and inside myself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语所有格的缩短形式，较长的形态仍以 mine 以及 myself 的组成部分存活。

normal.en: Old English min became mi before consonants and my in modern spelling, so my and mine are two shapes of one word.
normal.cn: 古英语 min 在辅音前变成 mi，后来写作 my，所以 my 与 mine 是同一个词的两个形态。

normal.en: My must stand before a noun; standing alone it becomes mine: my book, but the book is mine.
normal.cn: my 必须放在名词前；单独使用要变 mine：说 my book，但说 the book is mine。

normal.en: My takes no plural and no gender; unlike Latin meus, it never changes for the thing owned.
normal.cn: my 没有复数，也不分性别；不像拉丁语 meus，它从不随被拥有之物变形。

normal.en: My goodness and my word are fixed exclamations, not statements about owning anything.
normal.cn: my goodness 与 my word 是固定的感叹语，不是在陈述拥有什么。

normal.en: In my dear and my lord the word marks closeness or rank, a use that goes back to forms of address.
normal.cn: 在 my dear 与 my lord 里，这个词标记亲近或身份，这种用法来自称呼语。

abstract.en: A hand pressed to the chest says ownership is measured from the speaker outward.
abstract.cn: 一只手按在胸前，说明「所有」是从说话人向外量出来的。

abstract.en: A single letter added to a name turns a person into a position in someone else's life.
abstract.cn: 一个称呼前加上这个词，就把一个人变成了另一个人生活里的位置。

abstract.en: English possessives are short because the speaker is never far from what is claimed.
abstract.cn: 英语的所有格都很短，因为说话人离自己所声称的东西从来不远。

examples.en: My notes are on the kitchen table.
examples.cn: 我的笔记在厨房桌上。

examples.en: My grandmother taught me to sew.
examples.cn: 我外婆教我缝纫。

examples.en: I have lost my keys again.
examples.cn: 我又把钥匙弄丢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买」——my 读音近「买」，我的东西都是我买的。

root: 古英语 min（我的，第一人称属格）缩短为 my；与拉丁语 meus、希腊语词干 me- 同出原始印欧语第一人称词干。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ownership anchored in the speaker; the other senses stretch that anchor into exclamations and forms of address.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「以说话人为锚点的所有」；其余义项把这个锚点伸向感叹语与称呼语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing an object to the chest, marking it as mine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把物件按在胸前，标记它归我。

branches.en: a blue coat claimed at the door
branches.cn: 在门口被认领的蓝色外套

branches.en: a name written on a school bag
branches.cn: 写在书包上的名字

branches.en: hands raised at a near miss
branches.cn: 险些出事时抬起的手

branches.en: a breath let out after a shock
branches.cn: 受惊之后呼出的一口气

branches.en: a greeting spoken to an old friend
branches.cn: 对老朋友说出的问候

intro.en: The word is one short English form of a possessive stem that also yields the standalone form and the reflexive.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语所有格词干的一个短形态，同一词干还产出单独使用的形式和反身代词。

latinIntro.en: Latin carries the same first person stem in its possessive, which inflects for gender where English my does not.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的所有格带着同一个第一人称词干，并且随性别变化，而英语的 my 不变。

definition_zh: 我自己；我本人；独自
definition_en: the reflexive pronoun for the speaker, used when the speaker is the object, for emphasis, or in the phrase by myself meaning alone
core_image: 镜子里的人抬手，镜外的手也同时抬起，两边是同一个人
scene: 厨房里，砧板和菜刀摆在水池边，洋葱刚切到一半。I cut myself while chopping onions for dinner.
sceneCN: 这里是「我自己」（第 1 个义项：反身用法，动作回到主语本身）；句意为切洋葱做晚饭时我割伤了自己。图中可辨识物件：砧板、菜刀、洋葱。

derivatives.zh: myself 中的 self 部分，义为「自身、自我」
由 self 加 -ish 构成，义为「自私的」
由 self 加 -less 构成，义为「无私的」

senses.title: The speaker as the object of his own action
senses.definition: used as the object when the subject and the object are the same speaker
senses.definitionCN: 主语和宾语是同一个人（说话人）时用作宾语
senses.example: I cut myself while chopping onions for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 切洋葱做晚饭时我割伤了自己。
senses.why: English marks a returning action with a compound of the owner word and self, so the doer appears a second time inside the sentence as the one acted on.
senses.whyCN: 英语用「所有者词加 self」的复合形式标记回到自身的动作，于是动作发出者在句中第二次出现，成了被作用的人。

senses.title: The speaker, emphasized
senses.definition: used after a noun or at the end of a clause to stress that it was the speaker and no one else
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词后或句末，强调是说话人本人而不是别人
senses.example: I built these shelves myself.
senses.exampleCN: 这些架子是我自己搭的。
senses.why: The same compound can stand outside the verb's arguments and simply point at the speaker, which turns a reflexive into a spotlight.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合形式可以站在动词论元之外，单纯指向说话人，于是反身代词变成了一束追光。

senses.title: Alone, without company
senses.definition: used with by to say that the speaker is without other people
senses.definitionCN: 与 by 连用，表示身边没有别人
senses.example: I went to the cinema by myself.
senses.exampleCN: 我一个人去看了电影。
senses.why: If the speaker is the only one present, the returning self has no one else to lean on, so the reflexive phrase comes to mean solitude.
senses.whyCN: 如果只有说话人在场，那个回到自身的「我」没有别人可以依靠，反身短语于是引申出「独处」的意思。

intro.en: Myself joins the English possessive my to self, a Germanic word for one's own person that Old English already used in reflexive compounds.
intro.cn: myself 把英语所有格 my 与 self 结合；self 是日耳曼语中表示「自身」的词，古英语已用它构成反身复合形式。

items.en: A stem reconstructed as selbho- is often proposed for the reflexive family, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 常有人为这一族反身词提出重构形式 selbho-，但该重构并不确定。

items.en: The adjective selbaz meant the same person or the very one, and it supplied the base for self.
items.cn: 形容词 selbaz 意为「同一个人、正是那个人」，为 self 提供了基础。

items.en: Old English seolf or self could stand alone as a pronoun and appear in compounds with possessive forms.
items.cn: 古英语 seolf 或 self 可单独作代词，也能与所有格形式组合。

items.en: Middle English wrote combinations such as mi self as two words, and the pattern spread to every person of the pronoun.
items.cn: 中古英语把 mi self 这类组合写成两个词，这一模式扩展到人称代词的每一人称。

items.en: Modern English fused the parts into myself, added the emphatic and the by-phrase uses, and kept the plural pattern ourselves.
items.cn: 现代英语把两部分合并为 myself，发展出强调用法和 by 短语用法，并保留了复数形式 ourselves。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the parallel reflexives for other persons; the near-meaning group holds the bare pronouns and the idea of being alone.
note.cn: 形近组收其他人称的平行反身代词；近义组收不带 self 的代词以及「独自一人」这层意思。

entries.definition: The reflexive for the person spoken to, built the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 听话人的反身代词，构造方式相同。

entries.definition: The reflexive for a male third person.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称男性的反身代词。

entries.definition: The reflexive for we, with the plural selves.
entries.definitionCN: we 的反身代词，用复数形式 selves。

entries.definition: The reflexive for it, used for things and animals.
entries.definitionCN: it 的反身代词，用于事物和动物。

entries.definition: The plain object pronoun, used where the action does not return.
entries.definitionCN: 普通的宾格代词，动作不回到自身时使用。

entries.definition: The subject pronoun that myself points back to.
entries.definitionCN: 主格代词，myself 所指回的对象。

entries.definition: The general reflexive for an unspecified person.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某人的反身代词。

entries.definition: Without other people present, the sense carried by by myself.
entries.definitionCN: 身边没有别人，即 by myself 所表达的意思。

normalIntro.en: The word is my plus self, and the same recipe is repeated across the whole pronoun system.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 my 加 self，同一配方在人称代词的整套系统里反复使用。

normal.en: My plus self gives myself; the plural keeps the same recipe and changes my to our: ourselves.
normal.cn: my 加 self 得到 myself；复数沿用同一配方，把 my 换成 our，得到 ourselves。

normal.en: When the subject and the object are the same person, English uses the self form: I hurt myself, not I hurt me.
normal.cn: 主语和宾语是同一个人时，英语用带 self 的形式：说 I hurt myself，不说 I hurt me。

normal.en: Myself cannot be the subject of a finite verb; emphasis uses I myself or a final myself instead.
normal.cn: myself 不能充当限定动词的主语；要强调可以用 I myself，或把 myself 放在句末。

normal.en: By myself means alone; beside myself means out of control, not standing next to the body.
normal.cn: by myself 意为独自；beside myself 意为情绪失控，而不是站在身体旁边。

normal.en: In including myself, the self form works after a preposition or at the end of a list.
normal.cn: 在 including myself 里，这个反身形式用在介词后或列表末尾。

abstract.en: A mirror is the plainest picture of a sentence that turns back on its speaker.
abstract.cn: 镜子是一个句子折回说话人时最直白的画面。

abstract.en: A spotlight aimed at one person explains the emphatic use better than any rule.
abstract.cn: 一束只照一个人的追光，比任何规则都更能解释强调用法。

abstract.en: An empty cinema seat makes the meaning of by myself visible at once.
abstract.cn: 一个空着的电影院座位，一眼就能让人看见 by myself 的含义。

examples.en: I taught myself to play the guitar.
examples.cn: 我自学弹吉他。

examples.en: I painted the whole fence myself.
examples.cn: 整道栅栏都是我自己刷的。

examples.en: I waited by myself for over an hour.
examples.cn: 我独自等了一个多小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买赛尔夫」——自己给自己买东西，就叫 myself，我自己。

root: my 与古英语 self（自身）复合而成；self 一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 selbaz，拉丁语 ipse 只是意义相近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the speaker turning back on the speaker; emphasis and solitude are two ways that turn becomes visible.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是说话人把动作折回自己；强调用法与独处义，是这一折返的两种显形方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised before a mirror, with the reflected hand rising at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜前抬起一只手，镜中的手在同一刻也抬起。

branches.en: a cut finger held under the tap
branches.cn: 在水龙头下按住割伤的手指

branches.en: a sentence whose object is its subject
branches.cn: 宾语与主语是同一个人的句子

branches.en: a shelf built without help
branches.cn: 没有帮手也照样搭好的架子

branches.en: a ticket bought for one seat only
branches.cn: 只买了一个座位的票

branches.en: an empty row in a dark cinema
branches.cn: 黑暗影院里空着的一排座位

intro.en: The word is a compound of the possessive my and the Germanic self, and the same pieces recur in every reflexive pronoun.
intro.cn: 这个词由所有格 my 与日耳曼语的 self 复合而成，同样的部件在每个人称的反身代词中都会重现。

latinIntro.en: Latin has a reflexive pronoun of its own, but no form of it is a reliable source for self, so the cognate list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语有自己的反身代词，但其中没有任何形式可以可靠地作为 self 的来源，因此同源词列表留空。

items.meaning: the speaker as object or emphasis
